we see that \( {\int }_{{I}^{\prime } \times  \left\{  {t}^{\prime }\right\}  }{\left| Z\right| }^{2}{dz} \leq  \left( {1 + {3\delta }}\right) {\ell }_{{h}^{\prime }}\left( {I}^{\prime }\right) \) . It follows that for any \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}_{3}}\right\rbrack \) we have

\[
{\int }_{{I}^{\prime }\times \{ t\} }{\left| Z\right| }^{2}{dz} \leq  \left( {1 + {3\delta }}\right) {l}_{{h}^{\prime }}\left( {I}^{\prime }\right)  + {C}^{\prime }\left( {\sqrt{\delta }r + \delta {r}^{3} + {\delta }^{3/2}{r}^{2}}\right) .
\]

Since \( {\left| Z\right| }^{2} \) is between \( \left( {1 - \delta }\right) \left( {1 + {\left| {f}_{z}\right| }_{{h}^{\prime }}^{2}}\right) \) and \( \left( {1 + \delta }\right) \left( {1 + {\left| {f}_{z}\right| }_{{h}^{\prime }}^{2}}\right) \) , we see that there is a constant \( {C}_{1}^{\prime \prime } \) depending only on the ambient curvature bound such that for any \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}_{3}}\right\rbrack \) , denoting by \( {\ell }_{{h}^{\prime }}\left( {I}^{\prime }\right) \) the length of \( {I}^{\prime } \) with respect to \( {h}^{\prime } \) , we have

\[
{\int }_{{I}^{\prime }\times \{ t\} }{\left| {f}_{z}\right| }_{{h}^{\prime }}^{2}{dz} \leq  {4\delta }{\ell }_{{h}^{\prime }}\left( {I}^{\prime }\right)  + {C}_{1}^{\prime \prime }\left( {\sqrt{\delta }r + \delta {r}^{3} + {\delta }^{3/2}{r}^{2}}\right) .
\]

Since \( \left( {0.8}\right) r \leq  {\ell }_{{h}^{\prime }}\left( {I}^{\prime }\right)  \leq  r < 1 \) , we see that provided that \( \delta \) is sufficiently small, for each \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}_{3}}\right\rbrack \) there is \( z\left( t\right)  \in  {I}^{\prime } \) such \( {\left| {f}_{z}\left( z\left( t\right) , t\right) \right| }_{{h}^{\prime }}^{2} \leq  2{C}_{1}^{\prime \prime }\sqrt{\delta } \) . If we have chosen \( \delta \) sufficiently small, this means that for each \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}_{3}}\right\rbrack \) there is \( z\left( t\right) \) such that \( {\left| {f}_{z}\left( z\left( t\right) , t\right) \right| }_{{h}^{\prime }} \leq  1/{20} \) . Since by Corollary 19.63 \( {\int }_{{I}^{\prime }\times \{ t\} }{kds} < \; 2{D}_{4}\sqrt{\delta } \) , provided that \( \delta \) is sufficiently small, it follows that for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}_{3}}\right\rbrack \) the curve \( {\left. {\gamma }_{t}\right| }_{{I}^{\prime }} \) is a graph of \( \left( {z, t}\right) \) and \( {\left| {f}_{z}\right| }_{{h}^{\prime }} < 1/{10} \) . But by construction either \( {t}_{3} = {t}_{2} \) or there is a point in \( \left( {z,{t}_{3}}\right)  \in  {I}^{\prime } \times  \left\{  {t}_{3}\right\} \) with \( {\left| {f}_{z}\left( z,{t}_{3}\right) \right| }_{{h}^{\prime }} = 1/{10} \) . Hence, it must be the case that \( {t}_{3} = {t}_{2} \) , and thus our graph curve flow is defined for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) and satisfies the derivative bound \( {\left| {f}_{z}\right| }_{{h}^{\prime }} < 1/{10} \) throughout the interval \( \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) .

8.4. Proof that \( {t}_{2} = {t}^{\prime } + \delta {r}^{2} \) . The last step is to show that the inequality \( {k}^{2} < 2/\left( {t - {t}^{\prime }}\right) \) holds for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime } + \delta {r}^{2}}\right\rbrack \) .

We fix a point \( {x}_{0} \) . We continue all the notation, assumptions and results of the previous section. That is to say, we lift the evolving family of curves to the tangent space \( {T}_{{x}_{0}}M \) using the exponential mapping, which is a local diffeomorphism. This tangent space is split as the product of the \( z \) -axis and B. On this coordinate system we have the evolving family of Riemannian metrics \( h\left( t\right) \) pulled back from the Ricci flow and also we have the Euclidean metric \( {h}^{\prime } \) from the metric \( h\left( {t}^{\prime }\right) \) on \( {T}_{{x}_{0}}M \) . We fix an interval \( {I}^{\prime } \) on the \( z \) -axis of \( {h}^{\prime } \) -length between \( \left( {0.8}\right) r \) and \( r \) . We choose \( {I}^{\prime } \) to be centered at \( {x}_{0} \) with respect to the \( z \) -coordinate. On \( {I}^{\prime } \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) we have the graph-flow which is reparameterization of the pullback of the curve-shrinking flow. The graph-flow is given as the graph of a function \( f \) with \( {\left| {f}_{z}\right| }_{{h}^{\prime }} < 1/{10} \) . The vector fields \( Z \) and \( Y \) are as in the last section.

We follow closely the discussion in Section 4 of [2] (pages 293-294). Since we are not working in a flat background, there are two differences: (i) we take covariant derivatives instead of ordinary derivatives and (ii) there are various correction terms from curvature, from covariant derivatives, and from the fact that \( Y \) is not equal to \( {\nabla }_{Z}Z/{\left| Z\right| }^{2} \) .

Notice that

\[
Z\left( \frac{Z\left( {\left| Z\right| }^{2}\right) }{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}}\right)  = \frac{{\left| Z\right| }_{zz}^{2}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}} - \frac{{\left( {\left| Z\right| }_{z}^{2}\right) }^{2}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{4}}
\]

\[
= \frac{{\left| Z\right| }_{zz}^{2}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}} - 4\langle Y, Z{\rangle }^{2} - 8\langle Y, Z\rangle \psi \left( Z\right) {\left| Z\right| }^{2} - 4{\psi }^{2}\left( Z\right) {\left| Z\right| }^{4}.
\]

Thus, it follows from Equation (19.11) that we have

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{\left| Z\right| }^{2} = \frac{{\left( {\left| Z\right| }^{2}\right) }_{zz}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}} - 2{\left| Z\right| }^{2}{\left| Y\right| }^{2} - 4\langle Z, Y{\rangle }^{2} + V,
\]

where \( \left| V\right|  \leq  {C}^{\prime }\left( {1 + \delta \left| Y\right| }\right) \) for a constant \( {C}^{\prime } \) depending only on the curvature bound of the ambient flow.

Similar computations show that

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{\left| Y\right| }^{2} = \frac{{\left( {\left| Y\right| }^{2}\right) }_{zz}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}} - \frac{2{\left| {\nabla }_{Z}Y\right| }^{2}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}} - \frac{4}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}}\left\langle  {\frac{{\nabla }_{Z}Z}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}}, Y}\right\rangle  \left\langle  {{\nabla }_{Z}Y, Z}\right\rangle
\]

\[
- 2\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Y, Y}\right)  + 2\frac{\operatorname{Rm}\left( {Y, Z, Y, Z}\right) }{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}} - 2\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{Y}\left( {\psi \left( Z\right) Z}\right) , Y}\right\rangle  .
\]

Of course,

\[
\left\langle  {\frac{{\nabla }_{Z}Z}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}}, Y}\right\rangle   = {\left| Y\right| }^{2} + \psi \left( Z\right) \langle Z, Y\rangle .
\]

Hence, putting all this together and using Claim 19.66 we have

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{\left| Y\right| }^{2} = \frac{{\left( {\left| Y\right| }^{2}\right) }_{zz}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}} - \frac{2{\left| {\nabla }_{Z}Y\right| }^{2}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}} - \frac{4{\left| Y\right| }^{2}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}}\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{Z}Y, Z}\right\rangle   + W,
\]

where

\[
\left| W\right|  \leq  {C}^{\prime }\left| Y\right| \left( {\left| Y\right|  + \delta \left| {{\nabla }_{Z}Y}\right| }\right)
\]

Now let us consider

\[
Q = \frac{{\left| Y\right| }^{2}}{2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}}.
\]

Notice that since \( {\left| {f}_{z}\right| }_{{h}^{\prime }} < 1/{10} \) , it follows that \( 1 - \delta  \leq  {\left| Z\right| }^{2} < \left( {1.01}\right) \left( {1 + \delta }\right) \) on all of \( \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) . We now follow the computations on p. 294 of [2], adding in the error terms.

\[
{Q}_{t} = \frac{{\left| Y\right| }_{t}^{2}}{\left( 2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}\right) } + \frac{{\left| Y\right| }^{2}{\left| Z\right| }_{t}^{2}}{{\left( 2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}\right) }^{2}} = \frac{{\left| Y\right| }_{zz}^{2}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}\left( {2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}}\right) } - \frac{2{\left| {\nabla }_{Z}Y\right| }^{2}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}\left( {2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}}\right) }
\]

\[
- \frac{4{\left| Y\right| }^{2}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}\left( {2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}}\right) }\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{Z}Y, Z}\right\rangle   + \frac{W}{\left( 2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}\right) } + \frac{{\left| Y\right| }^{2}{\left| Z\right| }_{zz}^{2}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}{\left( 2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}\right) }^{2}}
\]

\[
- \frac{2{\left| Z\right| }^{2}{\left.\parallel  Y\right| }^{4}}{{\left( 2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}\right) }^{2}} - \frac{4{\left| Y\right| }^{2}}{{\left( 2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}\right) }^{2}}\langle Z, Y{\rangle }^{2} + \frac{{\left| Y\right| }^{2}}{{\left( 2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}\right) }^{2}}V
\]

On the other hand,

\[
\frac{{Q}_{zz}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}} = \frac{{\left| Y\right| }_{zz}^{2}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}\left( {2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}}\right) } + \frac{{\left| Y\right| }^{2}{\left| Z\right| }_{zz}^{2}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}{\left( 2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}\right) }^{2}} + \frac{2{\left| Y\right| }_{z}^{2}{\left| Z\right| }_{z}^{2}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}{\left( 2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}\right) }^{2}} + \frac{2{\left| Y\right| }^{2}{\left( {\left| Z\right| }_{z}^{2}\right) }^{2}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}{\left( 2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}\right) }^{3}}.
\]

From Claim 19.65 we have

\[
{\left| Z\right| }_{z}^{2} = 2\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{Z}Z, Z}\right\rangle   = 2{\left| Z\right| }^{2}\langle Y, Z\rangle  + {2\psi }\left( Z\right) {\left| Z\right| }^{4}.
\]

Plugging in this expansion gives

\[
\frac{{Q}_{zz}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}} = \frac{{\left| Y\right| }_{zz}^{2}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}\left( {2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}}\right) } + \frac{{\left| Y\right| }^{2}{\left| Z\right| }_{zz}^{2}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}{\left( 2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}\right) }^{2}}
\]

\[
+ \frac{8\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{Z}Y, Y}\right\rangle  \langle Y, Z\rangle }{{\left( 2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}\right) }^{2}} + \frac{{8\psi }\left( z\right) {\left| Z\right| }^{2}\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{Z}Y, Y}\right\rangle  }{{\left( 2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}\right) }^{2}}
\]

\[
+ \frac{8{\left| Z\right| }^{2}{\left| Y\right| }^{2}\langle Y, Z{\rangle }^{2}}{{\left( 2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}\right) }^{3}} + \frac{{16\psi }\left( Z\right) {\left| Z\right| }^{4}{\left| Y\right| }^{2}\langle Y, Z\rangle }{{\left( 2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}\right) }^{3}} + \frac{8{\psi }^{2}\left( Z\right) {\left| Z\right| }^{6}{\left| Y\right| }^{2}}{{\left( 2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}\right) }^{3}}.
\]

Expanding, we have

\[
\frac{{Q}_{zz}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}} = \frac{{\left| Y\right| }_{zz}^{2}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}\left( {2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}}\right) } + \frac{{\left| Y\right| }^{2}{\left| Z\right| }_{zz}^{2}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}{\left( 2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}\right) }^{2}} + \frac{8\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{Z}Y, Y}\right\rangle  \langle Y, Z\rangle }{{\left( 2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}\right) }^{2}}
\]

\[
+ \frac{8{\left| Y\right| }^{2}{\left| Z\right| }^{2}\langle Y, Z{\rangle }^{2}}{{\left( 2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}\right) }^{3}} + U,
\]

where

\[
\left| U\right|  \leq  {C}^{\prime }\left( {{\left| Y\right| }^{2} + \delta \left| {{\nabla }_{Z}Y}\right| \left| Y\right|  + \delta {\left| Y\right| }^{3}}\right) .
\]

Comparing the formulas yields

\[
{Q}_{t} = \frac{{Q}_{zz}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}} - \frac{8\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{Z}Y, Y}\right\rangle  \langle Y, Z\rangle }{{\left( 2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}\right) }^{2}} - \frac{8{\left| Y\right| }^{2}{\left| Z\right| }^{2}\langle Y, Z{\rangle }^{2}}{{\left( 2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}\right) }^{3}}
\]

\[
- \frac{2{\left| {\nabla }_{Z}Y\right| }^{2}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}\left( {2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}}\right) } - \frac{4{\left| Y\right| }^{2}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}\left( {2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}}\right) }\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{Z}Y, Z}\right\rangle
\]

\[
- \frac{2{\left| Z\right| }^{2}{\begin{Vmatrix}Y\end{Vmatrix}}^{4}}{{\left( 2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}\right) }^{2}} - \frac{4{\left| Y\right| }^{2}}{{\left( 2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}\right) }^{2}}\langle Z, Y{\rangle }^{2} + A
\]

where

\[
\left| A\right|  \leq  {C}^{\prime }\left( {{\left| Y\right| }^{2} + \delta \left| {{\nabla }_{Z}Y}\right| \left| Y\right|  + \delta {\left| Y\right| }^{3}}\right) .
\]

Using item (4) of Claim 19.65 this leads to

\[
{Q}_{t} \leq  \frac{{Q}_{zz}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}} + \frac{8\left( {1 + {3\delta }}\right) {\left| Y\right| }^{2}\left| {f}_{z}\right| \left| {{\nabla }_{Z}Y}\right| }{{\left( 2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}\right) }^{2}} - \frac{4{\left| Y\right| }^{2}\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{Z}Y, Y}\right\rangle  }{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}\left( {2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}}\right) }
\]

\[
- \frac{2{\left| {\nabla }_{Z}Y\right| }^{2}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}\left( {2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}}\right) } - \frac{2{\left| Z\right| }^{2}{\left| Y\right| }^{4}}{{\left( 2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}\right) }^{2}} + \left| A\right| .
\]

Next, we have

Claim 19.67.

\[
\left| \left\langle  {{\nabla }_{Z}Y, Z}\right\rangle  \right|  \leq  \left( {\left| {f}_{z}\right| \left( {\left| {{\nabla }_{Z}Y}\right|  + {2\delta }\left| Y\right| }\right)  + \delta {\left| Z\right| }^{2}\left| Y\right| }\right) \left( {1 + \delta }\right) .
\]

Proof. Since \( Y = \left( {0,\phi }\right) \) for some function \( \phi \) , we have \( {\nabla }_{Z}Y = \left( {0,{\phi }_{z}}\right)  + \; \Gamma \left( {Z, Y}\right) \) and hence

\[
\left| {\left\langle  {\nabla }_{Z}Y, Z\right\rangle  }_{{h}^{\prime }}\right|  = \left| {\left\langle  {\nabla }_{Z}Y,\left( 1,{f}_{z}\right) \right\rangle  }_{{h}^{\prime }}\right|
\]

\[
\leq  \left| {\left\langle  {f}_{z},{\phi }_{z}\right\rangle  }_{{h}^{\prime }}\right|  + \left| {\left\langle  \Gamma \left( Z, Y\right) , Z\right\rangle  }_{{h}^{\prime }}\right|
\]

\[
\leq  {\left| {f}_{z}\right| }_{{h}^{\prime }}{\left| {\phi }_{z}\right| }_{{h}^{\prime }} + \delta {\left| Z\right| }^{2}\left| Y\right| .
\]

On the other hand \( {\nabla }_{Z}Y = \left( {0,{\phi }_{z}}\right)  + \Gamma \left( {Z, Y}\right) \) so that \( {\left| {\phi }_{z}\right| }_{{h}^{\prime }} \leq  \left| {{\nabla }_{Z}Y}\right|  + \delta \left| Z\right| \left| Y\right| \) . From this the claim follows.

Now for \( \delta  > 0 \) sufficiently small, using the fact that \( 1 - \delta  < {\left| Z\right| }^{2} < \; \left( {1 + \delta }\right) \left( {1.01}\right) \) we can rewrite this as

\[
{Q}_{t} \leq  \frac{{Q}_{zz}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}} + \frac{8\left( {1 + {3\delta }}\right) {\left| Y\right| }^{2}\left| {f}_{z}\right| \left| {{\nabla }_{Z}Y}\right| }{{\left( 2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}\right) }^{2}} + \frac{4{\left| Y\right| }^{2}\left| {\left( {1 + \delta }\right) \left| {{\nabla }_{Z}Y}\right| \left| {f}_{z}\right| }\right| }{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}\left( {2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}}\right) }
\]

\[
- \frac{2{\left| {\nabla }_{Z}Y\right| }^{2}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}\left( {2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}}\right) } - \frac{\left( {1.95}\right) {\left| Y\right| }^{4}}{{\left( 2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}\right) }^{2}} + \widetilde{A}
\]

where \( \widetilde{A} \leq  {C}^{\prime }\left( {{\left| Y\right| }^{2} + \delta \left| Y\right| \left| {{\nabla }_{Z}Y}\right|  + \delta {\left| Y\right| }^{3}}\right) \) . Of course, \( \left| Y\right| \left| {{\nabla }_{Z}Y}\right|  + {\left| Y\right| }^{3} \leq \; 2{\left| Y\right| }^{2} + {\left| {\nabla }_{Z}Y\right| }^{2} + {\left| Y\right| }^{4} \) . Using this, provided that \( \delta \) is sufficiently small, we can rewrite this as

\[
{Q}_{t} \leq  \frac{{Q}_{zz}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}} + \frac{1}{\left( 2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}\right) } \cdot  \left\lbrack  \frac{8\left( {1 + {3\delta }}\right) \left| {{\nabla }_{Z}Y}\right| \left| {f}_{z}\right| {\left| Y\right| }^{2} - \left( {0.9}\right) {\left| Y\right| }^{4}}{\left( 2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}\right) }\right.
\]

\[
+ \frac{4{\left| Y\right| }^{2}\left| {\left( {1 + \delta }\right) \left| {{\nabla }_{Z}Y}\right| \left| {f}_{z}\right|  - \left( {1.9}\right) {\left| {\nabla }_{Z}Y\right| }^{2}}\right| }{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}} - {Q}^{2} + {\widetilde{A}}^{\prime \prime }
\]

where \( {\widetilde{A}}^{\prime \prime } \leq  {C}^{\prime }\left( {\left| Y\right| }^{2}\right) \) . We denote the quantity within the brackets by \( B \) and we estimate

\[
B \leq  8\left( {1 + {3\delta }}\right) \frac{{\left| Y\right| }^{2}\left| {{\nabla }_{Z}Y}\right| \left( {1/{10}}\right) \left( {1 + \delta }\right) }{\left( 2 - \left( {1.01}\right) \left( 1 + \delta \right) \right) } + \frac{4\left( {1/{10}}\right) \left( {1 + \delta }\right) {\left| Y\right| }^{2}\left| {{\nabla }_{Z}Y}\right| }{\left( 1 - \delta \right) }
\]

\[
- \frac{\left( {1.9}\right) }{\left( {1.01}\right) \left( {1 + \delta }\right) }{\left| {\nabla }_{Z}Y\right| }^{2} - \frac{\left( {0.9}\right) {\left| Y\right| }^{4}}{2 - \left( {1.01}\right) \left( {1 + \delta }\right) }
\]

\[
\leq  \left( {1.6}\right) {\left| Y\right| }^{2}\left| {{\nabla }_{Z}Y}\right|  - \left( {0.8}\right) {\left| {\nabla }_{Z}Y\right| }^{2} - \left( {0.8}\right) {\left| Y\right| }^{4}
\]

\[
\leq  0\text{ . }
\]

Therefore,

\[
{Q}_{t} \leq  \frac{{Q}_{zz}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}} - {Q}^{2} + \left| \widetilde{A}\right|  \leq  \frac{{Q}_{zz}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}} - {\left( Q - {C}_{1}^{\prime }\right) }^{2} + {\left( {C}_{1}^{\prime }\right) }^{2},
\]

for some constant \( {C}_{1}^{\prime } > 1 \) depending only on the curvature bound for the ambient Ricci flow.

Denote by \( l \) the length of \( {I}^{\prime } \) under \( {h}^{\prime } \) . As we have already seen, \( \left( {0.8}\right) r \leq \; l \leq  r \) . We translate the \( z \) -coordinate so that \( z = 0 \) is one endpoint of \( {I}^{\prime } \) and \( z = l \) is the other endpoint; the point \( {x}_{0} \) then corresponds to \( z = l/2 \) . Consider the function \( g = {l}^{2}/\left( {{z}^{2}{\left( l - z\right) }^{2}}\right) \) on \( {I}^{\prime } \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) . Direct computation shows that \( {g}_{zz} \leq  {12}{g}^{2} \) . Now set

\[
\widetilde{Q} = Q - {C}_{1}^{\prime }
\]

and

\[
h = \frac{1}{t - {t}^{\prime }} + \frac{4{\left( 1 - \delta \right) }^{-1}{l}^{2}}{{z}^{2}{\left( l - z\right) }^{2}} + {C}_{1}^{\prime }.
\]

Then

\[
- {h}_{t} + {\left( 1 - \delta \right) }^{-1}{h}_{zz} + {\left( {C}_{1}^{\prime }\right) }^{2} \leq  {h}^{2},
\]

so that

\[
{\left( \widetilde{Q} - h\right) }_{t} \leq  \frac{{\widetilde{Q}}_{zz}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}} - \frac{{h}_{zz}}{1 - \delta } - {\widetilde{Q}}^{2} + {h}^{2}.
\]

Since both \( h \) and \( {h}_{zz} \) are positive, at any point where \( \widetilde{Q} - h \geq  0 \) and \( {\widetilde{Q}}_{zz} < 0 \) , we have \( {\left( \widetilde{Q} - h\right) }_{t} < 0 \) . At any point where \( {Q}_{zz} \geq  0 \) , using the fact that \( {\left| Z\right| }^{2} \geq  \left( {1 - \delta }\right) \) we have

\[
{\left( \widetilde{Q} - h\right) }_{t} \leq  {\left( 1 - \delta \right) }^{-1}{\left( \widetilde{Q} - h\right) }_{zz} - {\widetilde{Q}}^{2} + {h}^{2}.
\]

Thus, for any fixed \( t \) , at any local maximum for \( \left( {\widetilde{Q} - h}\right) \left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) at which \( \left( {\widetilde{Q} - h}\right) \) is \( \geq  0 \) we have \( {\left( \widetilde{Q} - h\right) }_{t} \leq  0 \) . Since \( \widetilde{Q} - h \) equals \( - \infty \) at the end points of \( {I}^{\prime } \) for all times, there is a continuous function \( f\left( t\right)  = \mathop{\max }\limits_{{z \in  {I}^{\prime }}}\left( {\widetilde{Q} - h}\right) \left( {z, t}\right) \) , defined for all \( t \in  \left( {{t}^{\prime },{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) approaching \( - \infty \) uniformly as \( t \) approaches \( {t}^{\prime } \) from above. By the previous discussion, at any point where \( f\left( t\right)  \geq  0 \) we have \( {f}^{\prime }\left( t\right)  \leq  0 \) in the sense of forward difference quotients. It now follows that \( f\left( t\right)  \leq  0 \) for all \( t \in  \left( {{t}^{\prime },{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) . This means that for all \( t \in  \left( {{t}^{\prime },{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) at the \( {h}^{\prime } \) -midpoint \( {x}_{0} \) of \( {I}^{\prime } \) (the point where \( z = l/2 \) ) we have

\[
Q\left( {{x}_{0}, t}\right)  \leq  \frac{1}{t - {t}^{\prime }} + \frac{{16} \cdot  4{\left( 1 - \delta \right) }^{-1}}{{l}^{2}} + {C}_{1}^{\prime }.
\]

Since \( l \geq  \left( {0.8}\right) r \) and since \( t - {t}^{\prime } \leq  \delta {r}^{2} \) , we see that provided \( \delta \) is sufficiently small (depending on the bound of the curvature of the ambient flow) we have

\[
Q\left( {{x}_{0}, t}\right)  < \frac{3}{2\left( {t - {t}^{\prime }}\right) }
\]

for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) . Of course, since \( {\left| Z\right| }^{2} \geq  1 - \delta \) everywhere, this shows that

\[
{k}^{2}\left( {{x}_{0}, t}\right)  \leq  {\left| Y\left( {x}_{0}, t\right) \right| }^{2} = \left( {2 - {\left| Z\left( {x}_{0}, t\right) \right| }^{2}}\right) Q\left( {{x}_{0}, t}\right)  < \frac{2}{\left( t - {t}^{\prime }\right) }
\]

for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) . Since \( {x}_{0} \) was an arbitrary point of \( c\left( {\cdot ,{t}^{\prime }}\right) \) , this shows that \( k\left( {x, t}\right)  < \sqrt{\frac{2}{t - {t}^{\prime }}} \) for all \( x \in  c\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) and all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) . By the definition of \( {t}_{2} \) this implies that \( {t}_{2} = {t}^{\prime } + \delta {r}^{2} \) and completes the proof of Lemma 19.58.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
(Long-time behavior of the Ricci flow with surgery). Let \( w > \) 0 and \( 0 < \varepsilon  \leq  \frac{1}{2}w \) be any small positive constants and let \( \left( {{M}_{t},{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) }\right) ,0 < t < \; + \infty \) , be a solution to the Ricci flow with surgery, constructed by Theorem 7.4.3 with the nonincreasing (continuous) positive functions \( \widetilde{\delta }\left( t\right) \) and \( \widetilde{r}\left( t\right) \) and with a compact, orientable, irreducible and normalized three-manifold \( M \) as initial data, where each \( \delta \) -cutoff at a time \( t \) has \( \delta  = \delta \left( t\right)  \leq  \min \{ \widetilde{\delta }\left( t\right) ,\widetilde{r}\left( {2t}\right) \} \) . Then one of the following holds: either

(i) for all sufficiently large \( t \) , we have \( {M}_{t} = {M}_{\text{ thin }}\left( {w, t}\right) \) ; or

(ii) there exists a sequence of times \( {t}^{\alpha } \rightarrow   + \infty \) such that the scalings of \( {g}_{ij}\left( {t}^{\alpha }\right) \) on the essential component \( {M}_{{t}^{\alpha }}^{\left( 1\right) } \) , with factor \( {\left( {t}^{\alpha }\right) }^{-1} \) , converge in the \( {C}^{\infty } \) topology to a hyperbolic metric on the initial compact manifold \( M \) with constant sectional curvature \( - \frac{1}{4} \) ; or

(iii) we can find a finite collection of complete noncompact hyperbolic three-manifolds \( {\mathcal{H}}_{1},\ldots ,{\mathcal{H}}_{m} \) , with finite volume, and compact subsets \( {K}_{1},\ldots ,{K}_{m} \) of \( {\mathcal{H}}_{1},\ldots ,{\mathcal{H}}_{m} \) respectively obtained by truncating each cusp of the hyperbolic manifolds along constant mean curvature torus of small area, and for all t beyond some time \( T <  + \infty \) we can find diffeomorphisms \( {\varphi }_{l},1 \leq  l \leq  m \) , of \( {K}_{l} \) into \( {M}_{t} \) so that as long as \( t \) is sufficiently large, the metric \( {t}^{-1}{\varphi }_{l}^{ * }\left( t\right) {g}_{ij}\left( t\right) \) is as close to the hyperbolic metric as we like on the compact sets \( {K}_{1},\ldots ,{K}_{m} \) ; moreover, the complement \( {M}_{t} \smallsetminus  \left( {{\varphi }_{1}\left( {K}_{1}\right)  \cup  \cdots  \cup  {\varphi }_{m}\left( {K}_{m}\right) }\right) \) is contained in the thin part \( {M}_{\text{ thin }}\left( {w, t}\right) \) , and the boundary tori of each \( {K}_{l} \) are incompressible in the sense that each \( {\varphi }_{l} \) injects \( {\pi }_{1}\left( {\partial {K}_{l}}\right) \) into \( {\pi }_{1}\left( {M}_{t}\right) \) .

The proof of the theorem follows, with some modifications, essentially from the same argument of Hamilton as in the proof of Theorem 5.3.4.

Clearly we may assume that the thick part \( {M}_{\text{ thick }}\left( {w, t}\right) \) is not empty for a sequence \( {t}^{\alpha } \rightarrow   + \infty \) , since otherwise we have case (i). If we take a sequence of points \( {x}^{\alpha } \in \; {M}_{\text{ thick }}\left( {w,{t}^{\alpha }}\right) \) , then by Theorem 7.6.3(b) the scalings of \( {g}_{ij}\left( {t}^{\alpha }\right) \) around \( {x}^{\alpha } \) with factor \( {\left( {t}^{\alpha }\right) }^{-1} \) converge smoothly, along a subsequence of \( \alpha  \rightarrow   + \infty \) , to a complete hyperbolic manifold of finite volume with constant sectional curvature \( - \frac{1}{4} \) . The limits may be different for different choices of \( \left( {{x}^{\alpha },{t}^{\alpha }}\right) \) . If a limit is compact, we have case (ii). Thus we assume that all limits are noncompact.

Consider all the possible hyperbolic limits of the solution, and among them choose one such complete noncompact hyperbolic three-manifold \( \mathcal{H} \) with the least possible number of cusps. Denote by \( {h}_{ij} \) the hyperbolic metric of \( \mathcal{H} \) . For all small \( a > 0 \) we can truncate each cusp of \( \mathcal{H} \) along a constant mean curvature torus of area \( a \) which is uniquely determined; we denote the remainder by \( {\mathcal{H}}_{a} \) . Fix \( a > 0 \) so small that Lemma 5.3.7 is applicable for the compact set \( \mathcal{K} = {\mathcal{H}}_{a} \) . Pick an integer \( {l}_{0} \) sufficiently large and an \( {\epsilon }_{0} \) sufficiently small to guarantee from Lemma 5.3.8 that the identity map \( {Id} \) is the only harmonic map \( F \) from \( {\mathcal{H}}_{a} \) to itself with taking \( \partial {\mathcal{H}}_{a} \) to itself, with the normal derivative of \( F \) at the boundary of the domain normal to the boundary of the target, and with \( {d}_{{C}^{{l}_{0}}\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{a}\right) }\left( {F,{Id}}\right)  < {\epsilon }_{0} \) . Then choose a positive integer \( {q}_{0} \) and a small number \( {\delta }_{0} > 0 \) from Lemma 5.3.7 such that if \( \widetilde{F} \) is a diffeomorphism of \( {\mathcal{H}}_{a} \) into another complete noncompact hyperbolic three-manifold \( \left( {\widetilde{\mathcal{H}},{\widetilde{h}}_{ij}}\right) \) with no fewer cusps (than \( \mathcal{H} \) ), of finite volume and satisfying

\[
{\begin{Vmatrix}{\widetilde{F}}^{ * }{\widetilde{h}}_{ij} - {h}_{ij}\end{Vmatrix}}_{{C}^{{q}_{0}}\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{a}\right) } \leq  {\delta }_{0},
\]

then there exists an isometry \( I \) of \( \mathcal{H} \) to \( \widetilde{\mathcal{H}} \) such that

\[
{d}_{{C}^{{l}_{0}}\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{a}\right) }\left( {\widetilde{F}, I}\right)  < {\epsilon }_{0}.
\]

By Lemma 5.3.8 we further require \( {q}_{0} \) and \( {\delta }_{0} \) to guarantee the existence of a harmonic diffeomorphism from \( \left( {{\mathcal{H}}_{a},{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}}\right) \) to \( \left( {{\mathcal{H}}_{a},{h}_{ij}}\right) \) for any metric \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij} \) on \( {\mathcal{H}}_{a} \) with \( {\begin{Vmatrix}{\widetilde{g}}_{ij} - {h}_{ij}\end{Vmatrix}}_{{C}^{{q}_{0}}\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{a}\right) } \leq  {\delta }_{0}. \)

Let \( {x}^{\alpha } \in  {M}_{\text{ thick }}\left( {w,{t}^{\alpha }}\right) ,{t}^{\alpha } \rightarrow   + \infty \) , be a sequence of points such that the scalings of \( {g}_{ij}\left( {t}^{\alpha }\right) \) around \( {x}^{\alpha } \) with factor \( {\left( {t}^{\alpha }\right) }^{-1} \) converge to \( {h}_{ij} \) . Then there exist a marked point \( {x}^{\infty } \in  {\mathcal{H}}_{a} \) and a sequence of diffeomorphisms \( {F}_{\alpha } \) from \( {\mathcal{H}}_{a} \) into \( {M}_{{t}^{\alpha }} \) such that \( {F}_{\alpha }\left( {x}^{\infty }\right)  = {x}^{\alpha } \) and

\[
{\begin{Vmatrix}{\left( {t}^{\alpha }\right) }^{-1}{F}_{\alpha }^{ * }{g}_{ij}\left( {t}^{\alpha }\right)  - {h}_{ij}\end{Vmatrix}}_{{C}^{m}\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{a}\right) } \rightarrow  0
\]

as \( \alpha  \rightarrow  \infty \) for all positive integers \( m \) . By applying Lemma 5.3.8 and the implicit function theorem, we can change \( {F}_{\alpha } \) by an amount which goes to zero as \( \alpha  \rightarrow  \infty \) so as to make \( {F}_{\alpha } \) a harmonic diffeomorphism taking \( \partial {\mathcal{H}}_{a} \) to a constant mean curvature hypersurface \( {F}_{\alpha }\left( {\partial {\mathcal{H}}_{a}}\right) \) of \( \left( {{M}_{{t}^{\alpha }},{\left( {t}^{\alpha }\right) }^{-1}{g}_{ij}\left( {t}^{\alpha }\right) }\right) \) with the area \( a \) and satisfying the free boundary condition that the normal derivative of \( {F}_{\alpha } \) at the boundary of the domain is normal to the boundary of the target; and by combining with Lemma 7.6.2 (iii), we can smoothly continue each harmonic diffeomorphism \( {F}_{\alpha } \) forward in time a little to a family of harmonic diffeomorphisms \( {F}_{\alpha }\left( t\right) \) from \( {\mathcal{H}}_{a} \) into \( {M}_{t} \) with the metric \( {t}^{-1}{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) \) , with \( {F}_{\alpha }\left( {t}^{\alpha }\right)  = {F}_{\alpha } \) and with the time \( t \) slightly larger than \( {t}^{\alpha } \) , where \( {F}_{\alpha }\left( t\right) \) takes \( \partial {\mathcal{H}}_{a} \) into a constant mean curvature hypersurface of \( \left( {{M}_{t},{t}^{-1}{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) }\right) \) with the area \( a \) and also satisfies the free boundary condition. Moreover, since the surgeries do not take place at the points where the scalar curvature is negative, by the same argument as in Theorem 5.3.4 for an arbitrarily given positive integer \( q \geq  {q}_{0} \) , positive number \( \delta  < {\delta }_{0} \) , and sufficiently large \( \alpha \) , we can ensure the extension \( {F}_{\alpha }\left( t\right) \) satisfies \( {\begin{Vmatrix}{t}^{-1}{F}_{\alpha }^{ * }\left( t\right) {g}_{ij}\left( t\right)  - {h}_{ij}\end{Vmatrix}}_{{C}^{q}\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{a}\right) } \leq  \delta \) on a maximal time interval \( {t}^{\alpha } \leq  t \leq  {\omega }^{\alpha } \) (or \( {t}^{\alpha } \leq \; t < {\omega }^{\alpha } \) when \( {\omega }^{\alpha } =  + \infty ) \) , and with \( {\begin{Vmatrix}{\left( {\omega }^{\alpha }\right) }^{-1}{F}_{\alpha }^{ * }\left( {\omega }^{\alpha }\right) {g}_{ij}\left( {\omega }^{\alpha }\right)  - {h}_{ij}\end{Vmatrix}}_{{C}^{q}\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{a}\right) } = \delta \) , when \( {\omega }^{\alpha } <  + \infty \) . Here we have implicitly used the fact that \( {F}_{\alpha }\left( {\omega }^{\alpha }\right) \left( {\partial {\mathcal{H}}_{a}}\right) \) is still strictly concave to ensure the map \( {F}_{\alpha }\left( {\omega }^{\alpha }\right) \) is diffeomorphic.

We further claim that there must be some \( \alpha \) such that \( {\omega }^{\alpha } =  + \infty \) ; in other words, at least one hyperbolic piece persists. Indeed, suppose that for each large enough \( \alpha \) we can only continue the family \( {F}_{\alpha }\left( t\right) \) on a finite interval \( {t}^{\alpha } \leq  t \leq  {\omega }^{\alpha } <  + \infty \) with

\[
{\begin{Vmatrix}{\left( {\omega }^{\alpha }\right) }^{-1}{F}_{\alpha }^{ * }\left( {\omega }^{\alpha }\right) {g}_{ij}\left( {\omega }^{\alpha }\right)  - {h}_{ij}\end{Vmatrix}}_{{C}^{q}\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{a}\right) } = \delta .
\]

Consider the new sequence of manifolds \( \left( {{M}_{{\omega }^{\alpha }},{g}_{ij}\left( {\omega }^{\alpha }\right) }\right) \) . Clearly by Lemma 7.6.1, the scalings of \( {g}_{ij}\left( {\omega }^{\alpha }\right) \) around the new origins \( {F}_{\alpha }\left( {\omega }^{\alpha }\right) \left( {x}^{\infty }\right) \) with factor \( {\left( {\omega }^{\alpha }\right) }^{-1} \) converge smoothly (by passing to a subsequence) to a complete noncompact hyperbolic three-manifold \( \widetilde{\mathcal{H}} \) with the metric \( {\widetilde{h}}_{ij} \) and the origin \( {\widetilde{x}}^{\infty } \) and with finite volume. By the choice of the old limit \( \mathcal{H} \) , the new limit \( \widetilde{\mathcal{H}} \) has at least as many cusps as \( \mathcal{H} \) . By the definition of convergence, we can find a sequence of compact subsets \( {\widetilde{U}}_{\alpha } \) exhausting \( \widetilde{\mathcal{H}} \) and containing \( {\widetilde{x}}^{\infty } \) , and a sequence of diffeomorphisms \( {\widetilde{F}}_{\alpha } \) of neighborhood of \( {\widetilde{U}}_{\alpha } \) into \( {M}_{{\omega }^{\alpha }} \) with \( {\widetilde{F}}_{\alpha }\left( {\widetilde{x}}^{\infty }\right)  = {F}_{\alpha }\left( {\omega }^{\alpha }\right) \left( {x}^{\infty }\right) \) such that for each compact subset \( \widetilde{U} \) of \( \widetilde{\mathcal{H}} \) and each integer \( m \) ,

\[
{\begin{Vmatrix}{\left( {\omega }^{\alpha }\right) }^{-1}{\widetilde{F}}_{\alpha }^{ * }\left( {g}_{ij}\left( {\omega }^{\alpha }\right) \right)  - {\widetilde{h}}_{ij}\end{Vmatrix}}_{{C}^{m}\left( \widetilde{U}\right) } \rightarrow  0
\]

as \( \alpha  \rightarrow   + \infty \) . Thus for sufficiently large \( \alpha \) , we have the map

\[
{G}_{\alpha } = {\widetilde{F}}_{\alpha }^{-1} \circ  {F}_{\alpha }\left( {\omega }^{\alpha }\right)  : \;{\mathcal{H}}_{a} \rightarrow  \widetilde{\mathcal{H}}
\]

such that

\[
{\begin{Vmatrix}{G}_{\alpha }^{ * }{\widetilde{h}}_{ij} - {h}_{ij}\end{Vmatrix}}_{{C}^{q}\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{a}\right) } < \widetilde{\delta }
\]

for any fixed \( \widetilde{\delta } > \delta \) . Then a subsequence of \( {G}_{\alpha } \) converges at least in the \( {C}^{q - 1}\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{a}\right) \) topology to a map \( {G}_{\infty } \) of \( {\mathcal{H}}_{a} \) into \( \widetilde{\mathcal{H}} \) which is a harmonic map from \( {\mathcal{H}}_{a} \) into \( \widetilde{\mathcal{H}} \) and takes \( \partial {\mathcal{H}}_{a} \) to a constant mean curvature hypersurface \( {G}_{\infty }\left( {\partial {\mathcal{H}}_{a}}\right) \) of \( \left( {\mathcal{H},{h}_{ij}}\right) \) with the area \( a \) , as well as satisfies the free boundary condition. Clearly, \( {G}_{\infty } \) is at least a local diffeomorphism. Since \( {G}_{\infty } \) is the limit of diffeomorphisms, the only possibility of overlap is at the boundary. Note that \( {G}_{\infty }\left( {\partial {\mathcal{H}}_{a}}\right) \) is still strictly concave. So \( {G}_{\infty } \) is still a diffeomorphism. Moreover by using the standard regularity result of elliptic partial differential equations (see for example [48]), we also have

(7.6.20)

\[
{\begin{Vmatrix}{G}_{\infty }^{ * }{\widetilde{h}}_{ij} - {h}_{ij}\end{Vmatrix}}_{{C}^{q}\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{a}\right) } = \delta .
\]

Now by Lemma 5.3.7 we deduce that there exists an isometry \( I \) of \( \mathcal{H} \) to \( \widetilde{\mathcal{H}} \) with

\[
{d}_{{C}^{{l}_{0}}\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{a}\right) }\left( {{G}_{\infty }, I}\right)  < {\epsilon }_{0}.
\]

Thus \( {I}^{-1} \circ  {G}_{\infty } \) is a harmonic diffeomorphism of \( {\mathcal{H}}_{a} \) to itself which satisfies the free boundary condition and

\[
{d}_{{C}^{{l}_{0}}\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{a}\right) }\left( {{I}^{-1} \circ  {G}_{\infty },{Id}}\right)  < {\epsilon }_{0}.
\]

However the uniqueness in Lemma 5.3.8 concludes that \( {I}^{-1} \circ  {G}_{\infty } = {Id} \) which contradicts (7.6.20). So we have shown that at least one hyperbolic piece persists and the metric \( {t}^{-1}{F}_{\alpha }^{ * }\left( t\right) {g}_{ij}\left( t\right) \) , for \( {\omega }^{\alpha } \leq  t < \infty \) , is as close to the hyperbolic metric \( {h}_{ij} \) as we like.

We can continue to form other persistent hyperbolic pieces in the same way as long as there is a sequence of points \( {y}^{\beta } \in  {M}_{\text{ thick }}\left( {w,{t}^{\beta }}\right) ,{t}^{\beta } \rightarrow   + \infty \) , lying outside the chosen pieces. Note that \( V\left( t\right) {\left( t + \frac{3}{2}\right) }^{-\frac{3}{2}} \) is nonincreasing on \( \lbrack 0, + \infty ) \) . Therefore by combining with Margulis lemma (see for example [55] or [76]), we have proved that there exists a finite collection of complete noncompact hyperbolic three-manifolds \( {\mathcal{H}}_{1},\ldots ,{\mathcal{H}}_{m} \) with finite volume, a small number \( a > 0 \) and a time \( T <  + \infty \) such that for all \( t \) beyond \( T \) we can find diffeomorphisms \( {\varphi }_{l}\left( t\right) \) of \( {\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{l}\right) }_{a} \) into \( {M}_{t},1 \leq  l \leq  m \) , so that as long as \( t \) is sufficiently large, the metric \( {t}^{-1}{\varphi }_{l}^{ * }\left( t\right) {g}_{ij}\left( t\right) \) is as close to the hyperbolic metrics as we like and the complement \( {M}_{t} \smallsetminus  \left( {{\varphi }_{1}\left( t\right) \left( {\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{1}\right) }_{a}\right)  \cup  \cdots  \cup  {\varphi }_{m}\left( t\right) \left( {\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{m}\right) }_{a}\right) }\right) \) is contained in the thin part \( {M}_{\text{ thin }}\left( {w, t}\right) \) .

It remains to show the boundary tori of any persistent hyperbolic piece are incompressible. Let \( B \) be a small positive number and assume the above positive number \( a \) is much smaller than \( B \) . Let \( {M}_{a}\left( t\right)  = {\varphi }_{l}\left( t\right) \left( {\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{l}\right) }_{a}\right) \left( {1 \leq  l \leq  m}\right) \) be such a persistent hyperbolic piece of the manifold \( {M}_{t} \) truncated by boundary tori of area at with constant mean curvature, and denote by \( {M}_{a}^{c}\left( t\right)  = {M}_{t} \smallsetminus  {M}_{a}\left( t\right) \) the part of \( {M}_{t} \) exterior to \( {M}_{a}\left( t\right) \) . Thus there exists a family of subsets \( {M}_{B}\left( t\right)  \subset  {M}_{a}\left( t\right) \) which is a persistent hyperbolic piece of the manifold \( {M}_{t} \) truncated by boundary tori of area \( {Bt} \) with constant mean curvature. We also denote by \( {M}_{B}^{c}\left( t\right)  = {M}_{t} \smallsetminus  {\overset{ \circ  }{M}}_{B}\left( t\right) \) . By Van Kampen’s Theorem, if \( {\pi }_{1}\left( {\partial {M}_{B}\left( t\right) }\right) \) injects into \( {\pi }_{1}\left( {{M}_{B}^{c}\left( t\right) }\right) \) then it injects into \( {\pi }_{1}\left( {M}_{t}\right) \) also. Thus we only need to show \( {\pi }_{1}\left( {\partial {M}_{B}\left( t\right) }\right) \) injects into \( {\pi }_{1}\left( {{M}_{B}^{c}\left( t\right) }\right) \) .

As before we will use a contradiction argument to show \( {\pi }_{1}\left( {\partial {M}_{B}\left( t\right) }\right) \) injects into \( {\pi }_{1}\left( {{M}_{B}^{c}\left( t\right) }\right) \) . Let \( T \) be a torus in \( \partial {M}_{B}\left( t\right) \) and suppose \( {\pi }_{1}\left( T\right) \) does not inject into \( {\pi }_{1}\left( {{M}_{B}^{c}\left( t\right) }\right) \) . By Dehn’s Lemma we know that the kernel is a cyclic subgroup of \( {\pi }_{1}\left( T\right) \) generated by a primitive element. Consider the normalized metric \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}\left( t\right)  = {t}^{-1}{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) \) on \( {M}_{t} \) . Then by the work of Meeks-Yau [86] or Meeks-Simon-Yau [87], we know that among all disks in \( {M}_{B}^{c}\left( t\right) \) whose boundary curve lies in \( T \) and generates the kernel of \( {\pi }_{1}\left( T\right) \) , there is a smooth embedded disk normal to the boundary which has the least possible area (with respect to the normalized metric \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}\left( t\right) \) ). Denote by \( D \) the minimal disk and \( \widetilde{A} = \widetilde{A}\left( t\right) \) its area. We will show that \( \widetilde{A}\left( t\right) \) decreases at a certain rate which will arrive at a contradiction.

We first consider the case that there exist no surgeries at the time \( t \) . Exactly as in Part III of the proof of Theorem 5.3.4, the change of the area \( \widetilde{A}\left( t\right) \) comes from the change in the metric and the change in the boundary. For the change in the metric, we choose an orthonormal frame \( X, Y, Z \) at a point \( x \) in the disk \( D \) so that \( X \) and \( Y \) are tangent to the disk \( D \) while \( Z \) is normal. Since the normalized metric \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij} \) evolves by

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{\widetilde{g}}_{ij} =  - {t}^{-1}\left( {{\widetilde{g}}_{ij} + 2{\widetilde{R}}_{ij}}\right) ,
\]

the (normalized) area element \( d\widetilde{\sigma } \) of the disk \( D \) around \( x \) satisfies

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}d\widetilde{\sigma } =  - {t}^{-1}\left( {1 + \widetilde{\operatorname{Ric}}\left( {X, X}\right)  + \widetilde{\operatorname{Ric}}\left( {Y, Y}\right) }\right) d\widetilde{\sigma }.
\]

For the change in the boundary, we notice that the tensor \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij} + 2{\widetilde{R}}_{ij} \) is very small for the persistent hyperbolic piece. Then by using the Gauss-Bonnet theorem as before, we obtain the rate of change of the area

(7.6.21)

\[
\frac{d\widetilde{A}}{dt} \leq   - {\int }_{D}\left( {\frac{1}{t} + \frac{\widetilde{R}}{2t}}\right) d\widetilde{\sigma } + \frac{1}{t}{\int }_{\partial D}\widetilde{k}d\widetilde{s} - \frac{2\pi }{t} + o\left( \frac{1}{t}\right) \widetilde{L},
\]

where \( \widetilde{k} \) is the geodesic curvature of the boundary and \( \widetilde{L} \) is the length of the boundary curve \( \partial D \) (with respect to the normalized metric \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}\left( t\right) \) ). Since \( \widetilde{R} \geq   - {3t}/2\left( {t + \frac{3}{2}}\right) \) for all \( t \geq  0 \) by (7.6.2), the first term on the RHS of (7.6.21) is bounded above by

\[
- {\int }_{D}\left( {\frac{1}{t} + \frac{\widetilde{R}}{2t}}\right) d\widetilde{\sigma } \leq   - \frac{1}{t}\left( {\frac{1}{4} - o\left( 1\right) }\right) \widetilde{A}
\]

while the second term on the RHS of (7.6.21) can be estimated exactly as before by

\[
\frac{1}{t}{\int }_{\partial D}\widetilde{k}d\widetilde{s} \leq  \frac{1}{t}\left( {\frac{1}{4} + o\left( 1\right) }\right) \widetilde{L}.
\]

Thus we obtain

(7.6.22)

\[
\frac{d\widetilde{A}}{dt} \leq  \frac{1}{t}\left\lbrack  {\left( {\frac{1}{4} + o\left( 1\right) }\right) \widetilde{L} - \left( {\frac{1}{4} - o\left( 1\right) }\right) \widetilde{A} - {2\pi }}\right\rbrack  .
\]

Next we show that these arguments also work for the case that there exist surgeries at the time \( t \) . To this end, we only need to check that the embedded minimal disk \( D \) lies in the region which is unaffected by surgery. Our surgeries for the irreducible three-manifold took place on \( \delta \) -necks in \( \varepsilon \) -horns, where the scalar curvatures are at least \( {\delta }^{-2}{\left( \widetilde{r}\left( t\right) \right) }^{-1} \) , and the components with nonnegative scalar curvature have been removed. So the hyperbolic piece is not affected by the surgeries. In particular, the boundary \( \partial D \) is unaffected by the surgeries. Thus if surgeries occur on the minimal disk, the minimal disk has to pass through a long thin neck before it reaches the surgery regions. Look at the intersections of the embedding minimal disk with a generic center two-sphere \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \) of the long thin neck; these are circles. Since the two-sphere \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \) is simply connected, we can replace the components of the minimal disk \( D \) outside the center two-sphere \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \) by some corresponding components on the center two-sphere \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \) to form a new disk which also has \( \partial D \) as its boundary. Since the metric on the long thin neck is nearly a product metric, we could choose the generic center two-sphere \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \) properly so that the area of the new disk is strictly less than the area of the original disk \( D \) . This contradiction proves the minimal disk lies entirely in the region unaffected by surgery.

Since \( a \) is much smaller than \( B \) , the region within a long distance from \( \partial {M}_{B}\left( t\right) \) into \( {M}_{B}^{c}\left( t\right) \) will look nearly like a hyperbolic cusplike collar and is unaffected by the surgeries. So we can repeat the arguments in the last part of the proof of Theorem 5.3.4 to bound the length \( \widetilde{L} \) by the area \( \widetilde{A} \) and to conclude

\[
\frac{d\widetilde{A}}{dt} \leq   - \frac{\pi }{t}
\]

for all sufficiently large times \( t \) , which is impossible because the RHS is not integrable. This proves that the boundary tori of any persistent hyperbolic piece are incompressible.

Therefore we have proved the theorem. 0

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
(Justification of the canonical neighborhood assumption). Given any small \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) , there exist decreasing sequences \( 0 < {\widetilde{r}}_{j} < \varepsilon ,{\kappa }_{j} > 0 \) , and \( 0 < {\widetilde{\delta }}_{j} < {\varepsilon }^{2}, j = 1,2,\cdots \) , with the following property. Define the positive function \( \widetilde{\delta }\left( t\right) \) on \( \lbrack 0, + \infty ) \) by \( \widetilde{\delta }\left( t\right)  = {\widetilde{\delta }}_{j} \) for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {\left( {j - 1}\right) {\varepsilon }^{2}, j{\varepsilon }^{2}}\right) \) . Suppose there is a surgically modified solution, defined on \( \lbrack 0, T) \) with \( T <  + \infty \) , to the Ricci flow which satisfies the following:

(1) it starts on a compact orientable three-manifold with normalized initial metric, and

(2) it has only a finite number of surgeries such that each surgery at a time \( t \in  \left( {0, T}\right) \) is a \( \delta \left( t\right) \) -cutoff surgery with

\[
0 < \delta \left( t\right)  \leq  \min \{ \widetilde{\delta }\left( t\right) ,\bar{\delta }\left( t\right) \} .
\]

Then on each time interval \( \left\lbrack  {\left( {j - 1}\right) {\varepsilon }^{2}, j{\varepsilon }^{2}}\right\rbrack  \bigcap \lbrack 0, T), j = 1,2,\cdots \) , the solution satisfies the \( {\kappa }_{j} \) -noncollapsing condition on all scales less than \( \varepsilon \) and the canonical neighborhood assumption (with accuracy \( \varepsilon \) ) with \( r = {\widetilde{r}}_{j} \) .

Here and in the following, we call a (three-dimensional) surgically modified solution \( {g}_{ij}\left( t\right) ,0 \leq  t < T,\kappa \) -noncollapsed at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) on the scales less than \( \rho \) (for some \( \kappa  > 0,\rho  > 0 \) ) if it satisfies the following property: whenever \( r < \rho \) and

\[
\left| {{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  {r}^{-2}
\]

for all those \( \left( {x, t}\right)  \in  P\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}, r, - {r}^{2}}\right)  = \left\{  {\left( {{x}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime }}\right)  \mid  {x}^{\prime } \in  {B}_{{t}^{\prime }}\left( {{x}_{0}, r}\right) ,{t}^{\prime } \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0} - {r}^{2},{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack  }\right\} \) , for which the solution is defined, we have

\[
{\operatorname{Vol}}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0}, r}\right) }\right)  \geq  \kappa {r}^{3}.
\]

The proof of the proposition is by induction: having constructed our sequences for \( 1 \leq  j \leq  m \) , we make one more step, defining \( {\widetilde{r}}_{m + 1} \) , \( {\kappa }_{m + 1},{\widetilde{\delta }}_{m + 1} \) , and redefining \( {\widetilde{\delta }}_{m} = {\widetilde{\delta }}_{m + 1} \) . In view of the previous lemma, we only need to define \( {\widetilde{r}}_{m + 1} \) and \( {\widetilde{\delta }}_{m + 1} \) .

In Theorem 7.1.1 we have obtained the canonical neighborhood structure for smooth solutions. When adapting the arguments in the proof of Theorem 7.1.1 to the present surgical solutions, we will encounter the new difficulty of how to take a limit for the surgically modified solutions. The idea to overcome the difficulty consists of two parts. The first part, due to Perelman [104], is to choose \( {\widetilde{\delta }}_{m} \) and \( {\widetilde{\delta }}_{m + 1} \) small enough to push the surgical regions to infinity in space. (This is the reason why we need to redefine \( {\widetilde{\delta }}_{m} = {\widetilde{\delta }}_{m + 1} \) .) The second part is to show that solutions are smooth on some small, but uniform, time intervals (on compact subsets) so that we can apply Hamilton's compactness theorem, since we only have curvature bounds; otherwise Shi's interior derivative estimate may not be applicable. In fact, the second part is more crucial. That is just concerned with the question of whether the surgery times accumulate or not. Our argument will use the canonical neighborhood characterization of the standard solution in Lemma 7.3.5.

We now start to prove the proposition by contradiction. Suppose for sequence of positive numbers \( {r}^{\alpha } \) and \( {\widetilde{\delta }}^{\alpha \beta } \) , satisfying \( {r}^{\alpha } \rightarrow  0 \) as \( \alpha  \rightarrow  \infty \) and \( {\widetilde{\delta }}^{\alpha \beta } \leq  \frac{1}{\alpha  \cdot  \beta }\left( { \rightarrow  0}\right) \) , there exist sequences of solutions \( {g}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) to the Ricci flow with surgery, where each of them has only a finite number of cutoff surgeries and has a compact orientable normalized three-manifold as initial data, so that the following two assertions hold:

(i) each \( \delta \) -cutoff at a time \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {\left( {m - 1}\right) {\varepsilon }^{2},\left( {m + 1}\right) {\varepsilon }^{2}}\right\rbrack \) satisfies \( \delta  \leq  {\widetilde{\delta }}^{\alpha \beta } \) ; and

(ii) the solutions satisfy the statement of the proposition on \( \left\lbrack  {0, m{\varepsilon }^{2}}\right\rbrack \) , but violate the canonical neighborhood assumption (with accuracy \( \varepsilon \) ) with \( r = {r}^{\alpha } \) on \( \left\lbrack  {m{\varepsilon }^{2},\left( {m + 1}\right) {\varepsilon }^{2}}\right\rbrack \) .

For each solution \( {g}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) , we choose \( \bar{t} \) (depending on \( \alpha \) and \( \beta \) ) to be the nearly first time for which the canonical neighborhood assumption (with accuracy \( \varepsilon \) ) is violated. More precisely, we choose \( \bar{t} \in  \left\lbrack  {m{\varepsilon }^{2},\left( {m + 1}\right) {\varepsilon }^{2}}\right\rbrack \) so that the canonical neighborhood assumption with \( r = {r}^{\alpha } \) and with accuracy parameter \( \varepsilon \) is violated at some \( \left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) \) , however the canonical neighborhood assumption with accuracy parameter \( {2\varepsilon } \) holds on \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {m{\varepsilon }^{2},\bar{t}}\right\rbrack \) . After passing to subsequences, we may assume each \( {\widetilde{\delta }}^{\alpha \beta } \) is less than the \( \widetilde{\delta } \) in Lemma 7.4.2 with \( r = {r}^{\alpha } \) when \( \alpha \) is fixed. Then by Lemma 7.4.2 we have uniform \( \kappa \) -noncollapsing on all scales less than \( \varepsilon \) on \( \left\lbrack  {0,\bar{t}}\right\rbrack \) with some \( \kappa  > 0 \) independent of \( \alpha ,\beta \) .

Slightly abusing notation, we will often drop the indices \( \alpha \) and \( \beta \) .

Let \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) be the rescaled solutions around \( \left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) \) with factors \( R\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) \left( { \geq  {r}^{-2} \rightarrow   + \infty }\right) \) and shift the times \( \bar{t} \) to zero. We hope to take a limit of the rescaled solutions for subsequences of \( \alpha ,\beta  \rightarrow  \infty \) and show the limit is an orientable ancient \( \kappa \) -solution, which will give the desired contradiction. We divide our arguments into the following six steps.

Step 1. Let \( \left( {y,\widehat{t}}\right) \) be a point on the rescaled solution \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) with \( \widetilde{R}\left( {y,\widehat{t}}\right)  \leq  A \) (for some \( A \geq  1 \) ) and \( \widehat{t} \in  \left\lbrack  {-\left( {\bar{t} - \left( {m - 1}\right) {\varepsilon }^{2}}\right) R\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) ,0}\right\rbrack \) . Then we have estimate

(7.4.14)

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {10A}
\]

for those \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) in the parabolic neighborhood \( P\left( {y,\widehat{t},\frac{1}{2}{\eta }^{-1}{A}^{-\frac{1}{2}}, - \frac{1}{8}{\eta }^{-1}{A}^{-1}}\right)  \triangleq \; \left\{  {\left( {{x}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime }}\right)  \mid  {x}^{\prime } \in  {\widetilde{B}}_{{t}^{\prime }}\left( {y,\frac{1}{2}{\eta }^{-1}{A}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) ,{t}^{\prime } \in  \left\lbrack  {\widehat{t} - \frac{1}{8}{\eta }^{-1}{A}^{-1},\widehat{t}}\right\rbrack  }\right\} \) , for which the rescaled solution is defined.

Indeed, as in the first step of the proof of Theorem 7.1.1, this follows directly from the gradient estimates (7.3.4) in the canonical neighborhood assumption with parameter \( {2\varepsilon } \) .

Step 2. In this step, we will prove three time extension results.

Assertion 1. For arbitrarily fixed \( \alpha ,0 < A <  + \infty ,1 \leq  C <  + \infty \) and \( 0 \leq  B < \frac{1}{2}{\varepsilon }^{2}{\left( {r}^{\alpha }\right) }^{-2} - \frac{1}{8}{\eta }^{-1}{C}^{-1} \) , there is a \( {\beta }_{0} = {\beta }_{0}\left( {\varepsilon , A, B, C}\right) \) (independent of \( \alpha \) ) such that if \( \beta  \geq  {\beta }_{0} \) and the rescaled solution \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) on the ball \( {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right) \) is defined on a time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-b,0}\right\rbrack \) with \( 0 \leq  b \leq  B \) and the scalar curvature satisfies

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  C,\;\text{ on }{\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {-b,0}\right\rbrack  ,
\]

then the rescaled solution \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) on the ball \( {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right) \) is also defined on the extended time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-b - \frac{1}{8}{\eta }^{-1}{C}^{-1},0}\right\rbrack \) .

Before giving the proof, we make a simple observation: once a space point in the Ricci flow with surgery is removed by surgery at some time, then it never appears for later time; if a space point at some time \( t \) cannot be defined before the time \( t \) , then either the point lies in a gluing cap of the surgery at time \( t \) or the time \( t \) is the initial time of the Ricci flow.

Proof of Assertion 1. Firstly we claim that there exists \( {\beta }_{0} = {\beta }_{0}\left( {\varepsilon , A, B, C}\right) \) such that when \( \beta  \geq  {\beta }_{0} \) , the rescaled solution \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) on the ball \( {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right) \) can be defined before the time \( - b \) (i.e., there are no surgeries interfering in \( {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {-b - {\epsilon }^{\prime }, - b}\right\rbrack \) for some \( \left. {{\epsilon }^{\prime } > 0}\right) \) .

We argue by contradiction. Suppose not, then there is some point \( \widetilde{x} \in  {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right) \) such that the rescaled solution \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) at \( \widetilde{x} \) cannot be defined before the time \( - b \) . By the above observation, there is a surgery at the time \( - b \) such that the point \( \widetilde{x} \) lies in the instant gluing cap.

Let \( \widetilde{h}\left( { = R{\left( \bar{x},\bar{t}\right) }^{\frac{1}{2}}h}\right) \) be the cut-off radius at the time \( - b \) for the rescaled solution. Clearly, there is a universal constant \( D \) such that \( {D}^{-1}\widetilde{h} \leq  \widetilde{R}{\left( \widetilde{x}, - b\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}} \leq  D\widetilde{h} \) .

By Lemma 7.3.4 and looking at the rescaled solution at the time \( - b \) , the gluing cap and the adjacent \( \delta \) -neck, of radius \( \widetilde{h} \) , constitute a \( {\left( {\widetilde{\delta }}^{\alpha \beta }\right) }^{\frac{1}{2}} \) -cap \( \mathcal{K} \) . For any fixed small positive constant \( {\delta }^{\prime } \) (much smaller than \( \varepsilon \) ), we see that

\[
{\widetilde{B}}_{\left( -b\right) }\left( {\widetilde{x},{\left( {\delta }^{\prime }\right) }^{-1}\widetilde{R}{\left( \widetilde{x}, - b\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right)  \subset  \mathcal{K}
\]

when \( \beta \) large enough. We first verify the following

CLAIM 1. For any small constants \( 0 < \widetilde{\theta } < 1,{\delta }^{\prime } > 0 \) , there exists a \( \beta \left( {{\delta }^{\prime },\varepsilon ,\widetilde{\theta }}\right)  > 0 \) such that when \( \beta  \geq  \beta \left( {{\delta }^{\prime },\varepsilon ,\widetilde{\theta }}\right) \) , we have

(i) the rescaled solution \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) over \( {\widetilde{B}}_{\left( -b\right) }\left( {\widetilde{x},{\left( {\delta }^{\prime }\right) }^{-1}\widetilde{h}}\right) \) is defined on the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-b,0}\right\rbrack   \cap  \left\lbrack  {-b, - b + \left( {1 - \widetilde{\theta }}\right) {\widetilde{h}}^{2}}\right\rbrack \)

(ii) the ball \( {\widetilde{B}}_{\left( -b\right) }\left( {\widetilde{x},{\left( {\delta }^{\prime }\right) }^{-1}\widetilde{h}}\right) \) in the \( {\left( {\widetilde{\delta }}^{\alpha \beta }\right) }^{\frac{1}{2}} \) -cap \( \mathcal{K} \) evolved by the Ricci flow on the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-b,0}\right\rbrack   \cap  \left\lbrack  {-b, - b + \left( {1 - \widetilde{\theta }}\right) {\widetilde{h}}^{2}}\right\rbrack \) is, after scaling with factor \( {\widetilde{h}}^{-2} \) , \( {\delta }^{\prime } \) -close (in the \( {C}^{\left\lbrack  {\delta }^{\prime  - 1}\right\rbrack  } \) topology) to the corresponding subset of the standard solution.

This claim essentially follows from Lemma 7.3.6. Indeed, suppose there is a surgery at some time \( \widetilde{\widetilde{t}} \in  \left\lbrack  {-b,0}\right\rbrack   \cap  \left( {-b, - b + \left( {1 - \widetilde{\theta }}\right) {\widetilde{h}}^{2}}\right\rbrack \) which removes some point \( \widetilde{\widetilde{x}} \in  {\widetilde{B}}_{\left( -b\right) }\left( {\widetilde{x},{\left( {\delta }^{\prime }\right) }^{-1}\widetilde{h}}\right) \) . We assume \( \widetilde{\widetilde{t}} \in  ( - b,0\rbrack \) is the first time with that property.

Then by Lemma 7.3.6, there is a \( \bar{\delta } = \bar{\delta }\left( {{\delta }^{\prime },\varepsilon ,\widetilde{\theta }}\right) \) such that if \( {\widetilde{\delta }}^{\alpha \beta } < \bar{\delta } \) , then the ball \( {\widetilde{B}}_{\left( -b\right) }\left( {\widetilde{x},{\left( {\delta }^{\prime }\right) }^{-1}\widetilde{h}}\right) \) in the \( {\left( {\widetilde{\delta }}^{\alpha \beta }\right) }^{\frac{1}{2}} \) -cap \( \mathcal{K} \) evolved by the Ricci flow on the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-b,\widetilde{\widetilde{t}}}\right) \) is, after scaling with factor \( {\widetilde{h}}^{-2},{\delta }^{\prime } \) -close to the corresponding subset of the standard solution. Note that the metrics for times in \( \lbrack  - b,\widetilde{\widetilde{t}}) \) on \( {\widetilde{B}}_{\left( -b\right) }\left( {\widetilde{x},{\left( {\delta }^{\prime }\right) }^{-1}\widetilde{h}}\right) \) are equivalent. By Lemma 7.3.6, the solution on \( {\widetilde{B}}_{\left( -b\right) }\left( {\widetilde{x},{\left( {\delta }^{\prime }\right) }^{-1}\widetilde{h}}\right) \) keeps looking like a cap for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {-b,\widetilde{\widetilde{t}}}\right\rbrack \) . On the other hand, by the definition, the surgery is always done along the middle two-sphere of a \( \delta \) -neck with \( \delta  < {\widetilde{\delta }}^{\alpha \beta } \) . Then for \( \beta \) large, all the points in \( {\widetilde{B}}_{\left( -b\right) }\left( {\widetilde{x},{\left( {\delta }^{\prime }\right) }^{-1}\widetilde{h}}\right) \) are removed (as a part of a capped horn) at the time \( \widetilde{\widetilde{t}} \) . But \( \widetilde{x} \) (near the tip of the cap) exists past the time \( \widetilde{\widetilde{t}} \) . This is a contradiction. Hence we have proved that \( {\widetilde{B}}_{\left( -b\right) }\left( {\widetilde{x},{\left( {\delta }^{\prime }\right) }^{-1}\widetilde{h}}\right) \) is defined on the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-b,0}\right\rbrack   \cap  \left\lbrack  {-b, - b + \left( {1 - \widetilde{\theta }}\right) {\widetilde{h}}^{2}}\right\rbrack \) .

The \( {\delta }^{\prime } \) -closeness of the solution on \( {\widetilde{B}}_{\left( -b\right) }\left( {\widetilde{x},{\left( {\delta }^{\prime }\right) }^{-1}h}\right)  \times  \left( {\left\lbrack  {-b,0}\right\rbrack   \cap  \left\lbrack  {-b, - b + \left( {1 - \widetilde{\theta }}\right) {\widetilde{h}}^{2}}\right\rbrack  }\right) \) with the corresponding subset of the standard solution follows from Lemma 7.3.6. Then we have proved Claim 1.

We next verify the following

CLAIM 2. There is \( \widetilde{\theta } = \widetilde{\theta }\left( {CB}\right) ,0 < \widetilde{\theta } < 1 \) , such that \( b \leq  \left( {1 - \widetilde{\theta }}\right) {\widetilde{h}}^{2} \) when \( \beta \) large.

Note from Proposition 7.3.3, there is a universal constant \( {D}^{\prime } > 0 \) such that the standard solution satisfies the following curvature estimate

\[
R\left( {y, s}\right)  \geq  \frac{2{D}^{\prime }}{1 - s}.
\]

We choose \( \widetilde{\theta } = {D}^{\prime }/2\left( {{D}^{\prime } + {CB}}\right) \) . Then for \( \beta \) large enough, the rescaled solution satisfies

(7.4.15)

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {x, t}\right)  \geq  \frac{{D}^{\prime }}{1 - \left( {t + b}\right) {\widetilde{h}}^{-2}}{\widetilde{h}}^{-2}
\]

on \( {\widetilde{B}}_{\left( -b\right) }\left( {\widetilde{x},{\left( {\delta }^{\prime }\right) }^{-1}\widetilde{h}}\right)  \times  \left( {\left\lbrack  {-b,0}\right\rbrack   \cap  \left\lbrack  {-b, - b + \left( {1 - \widetilde{\theta }}\right) {\widetilde{h}}^{2}}\right\rbrack  }\right) \) .

Suppose \( b \geq  \left( {1 - \widetilde{\theta }}\right) {\widetilde{h}}^{2} \) . Then by combining with the assumption \( \widetilde{R}\left( {\widetilde{x}, t}\right)  \leq  C \) for \( t = \left( {1 - \widetilde{\theta }}\right) {\widetilde{h}}^{2} - b \) , we have

\[
C \geq  \frac{{D}^{\prime }}{1 - \left( {t + b}\right) {\widetilde{h}}^{-2}}{\widetilde{h}}^{-2},
\]

and then

\[
1 \geq  \left( {1 - \widetilde{\theta }}\right) \left( {1 + \frac{{D}^{\prime }}{CB}}\right) .
\]

This is a contradiction. Hence we have proved Claim 2.

The combination of the above two claims shows that there is a positive constant \( 0 < \widetilde{\theta } = \widetilde{\theta }\left( {CB}\right)  < 1 \) such that for any small \( {\delta }^{\prime } > 0 \) , there is a positive \( \beta \left( {{\delta }^{\prime },\varepsilon ,\widetilde{\theta }}\right) \) such that when \( \beta  \geq  \beta \left( {{\delta }^{\prime },\varepsilon ,\widetilde{\theta }}\right) \) , we have \( b \leq  \left( {1 - \widetilde{\theta }}\right) {\widetilde{h}}^{2} \) and the rescaled solution in the ball \( {\widetilde{B}}_{\left( -b\right) }\left( {\widetilde{x},{\left( {\delta }^{\prime }\right) }^{-1}\widetilde{h}}\right) \) on the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-b,0}\right\rbrack \) is, after scaling with factor \( {\widetilde{h}}^{-2},{\delta }^{\prime } \) -close (in the \( {C}^{\left\lbrack  {\left( {\delta }^{\prime }\right) }^{-1}\right\rbrack  } \) topology) to the corresponding subset of the standard solution.

By (7.4.15) and the assumption \( \widetilde{R} \leq  C \) on \( {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {-b,0}\right\rbrack \) , we know that the cut-off radius \( \widetilde{h} \) at the time \( - b \) for the rescaled solution satisfies

\[
\widetilde{h} \geq  \sqrt{\frac{{D}^{\prime }}{C}}.
\]

Let \( {\delta }^{\prime } > 0 \) be much smaller than \( \varepsilon \) and \( \min \left\{  {{A}^{-1}, A}\right\} \) . Since \( {\widetilde{d}}_{0}\left( {\widetilde{x},\bar{x}}\right)  \leq  A \) , it follows that there is constant \( C\left( \widetilde{\theta }\right) \) depending only on \( \widetilde{\theta } \) such that \( {\widetilde{d}}_{\left( -b\right) }\left( {\widetilde{x},\bar{x}}\right)  \leq  C\left( \widetilde{\theta }\right) A \ll \; {\left( {\delta }^{\prime }\right) }^{-1}\widetilde{h} \) . We now apply Lemma 7.3.5 with the accuracy parameter \( \varepsilon /2 \) . Let \( C\left( {\varepsilon /2}\right) \) be the positive constant in Lemma 7.3.5. Without loss of generality, we may assume the positive constant \( {C}_{1}\left( \varepsilon \right) \) in the canonical neighborhood assumption is larger than \( {4C}\left( {\varepsilon /2}\right) \) . When \( {\delta }^{\prime }\left( { > 0}\right) \) is much smaller than \( \varepsilon \) and \( \min \left\{  {{A}^{-1}, A}\right\} \) , the point \( \bar{x} \) at the time \( \bar{t} \) has a neighborhood which is either a \( \frac{3}{4}\varepsilon \) -cap or a \( \frac{3}{4}\varepsilon \) -neck.

Since the canonical neighborhood assumption with accuracy parameter \( \varepsilon \) is violated at \( \left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) \) , the neighborhood of the point \( \bar{x} \) at the new time zero for the rescaled solution must be a \( \frac{3}{4}\varepsilon \) -neck. By Lemma 7.3.5 (b), we know the neighborhood is the slice at the time zero of the parabolic neighborhood

\[
P\left( {\bar{x},0,\frac{4}{3}{\varepsilon }^{-1}\widetilde{R}{\left( \bar{x},0\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}, - \min \left\{  {\widetilde{R}{\left( \bar{x},0\right) }^{-1}, b}\right\}  }\right)
\]

(with \( \widetilde{R}\left( {\bar{x},0}\right)  = 1 \) ) which is \( \frac{3}{4}\varepsilon \) -close (in the \( {C}^{\left\lbrack  \frac{4}{3}{\varepsilon }^{-1}\right\rbrack  } \) topology) to the corresponding subset of the evolving standard cylinder \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \times  \mathbb{R} \) over the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-\min \{ b,1\} ,0}\right\rbrack \) with scalar curvature 1 at the time zero. If \( b \geq  1 \) , the \( \frac{3}{4}\varepsilon \) -neck is strong, which is a contradiction. While if \( b < 1 \) , the \( \frac{3}{4}\varepsilon \) -neck at time \( - b \) is contained in the union of the gluing cap and the adjacent \( \delta \) -neck where the \( \delta \) -cutoff surgery took place. Since \( \varepsilon \) is small (say \( \varepsilon  < 1/{100} \) ), it is clear that the point \( \bar{x} \) at time \( - b \) is the center of an \( \varepsilon \) -neck which is entirely contained in the adjacent \( \delta \) -neck. By the proof of Lemma 7.3.2, the adjacent \( \delta \) -neck approximates an ancient \( \kappa \) -solution. This implies the point \( \bar{x} \) at the time \( \bar{t} \) has a strong \( \varepsilon \) -neck, which is also a contradiction.

Hence we have proved that there exists \( {\beta }_{0} = {\beta }_{0}\left( {\varepsilon , A, B, C}\right) \) such that when \( \beta  \geq  {\beta }_{0} \) , the rescaled solution on the ball \( {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right) \) can be defined before the time \( - b \) .

Let \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{A}^{\alpha \beta },0}\right\rbrack   \supset  \left\lbrack  {-b,0}\right\rbrack \) be the largest time interval so that the rescaled solution \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) can be defined on \( {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{A}^{\alpha \beta },0}\right\rbrack \) . We finally claim that \( {t}_{A}^{\alpha \beta } \leq   - b - \frac{1}{8}{\eta }^{-1}{C}^{-1} \) for \( \beta \) large enough.

Indeed, suppose not, by the gradient estimates as in Step 1, we have the curvature estimate

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {10C}
\]

on \( {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{A}^{\alpha \beta }, - b}\right\rbrack \) . Hence we have the curvature estimate

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {10C}
\]

on \( {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{A}^{\alpha \beta },0}\right\rbrack \) . By the above argument there is a \( {\beta }_{0} = {\beta }_{0}(\varepsilon , A, B + \; \left. {\frac{1}{8}{\eta }^{-1}{C}^{-1},{10C}}\right) \) such that for \( \beta  \geq  {\beta }_{0} \) , the solution in the ball \( {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right) \) can be defined before the time \( {t}_{A}^{\alpha \beta } \) . This is a contradiction.

Therefore we have proved Assertion 1.

Assertion 2. For arbitrarily fixed \( \alpha ,0 < A <  + \infty ,1 \leq  C <  + \infty \) and \( 0 < B < \frac{1}{2}{\varepsilon }^{2}{\left( {r}^{\alpha }\right) }^{-2} - \frac{1}{50}{\eta }^{-1} \) , there is a \( {\beta }_{0} = {\beta }_{0}\left( {\varepsilon , A, B, C}\right) \) (independent of \( \alpha \) ) such that if \( \beta  \geq  {\beta }_{0} \) and the rescaled solution \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) on the ball \( {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right) \) is defined on a time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-b + {\epsilon }^{\prime },0}\right\rbrack \) with \( 0 < b \leq  B \) and \( 0 < {\epsilon }^{\prime } < \frac{1}{50}{\eta }^{-1} \) and the scalar curvature satisfies

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  C\;\text{ on }{\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {-b + {\epsilon }^{\prime },0}\right\rbrack  ,
\]

and there is a point \( y \in  {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right) \) such that \( \widetilde{R}\left( {y, - b + {\epsilon }^{\prime }}\right)  \leq  \frac{3}{2} \) , then the rescaled solution \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) at \( y \) is also defined on the extended time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-b - \frac{1}{50}{\eta }^{-1},0}\right\rbrack \) and satisfies the estimate

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {y, t}\right)  \leq  {15}
\]

for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {-b - \frac{1}{50}{\eta }^{-1}, - b + {\epsilon }^{\prime }}\right\rbrack \) .

Proof of Assertion 2. We imitate the proof of Assertion 1. If the rescaled solution \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) at \( y \) cannot be defined for some time in \( \left\lbrack  {-b - \frac{1}{50}{\eta }^{-1}, - b + {\epsilon }^{\prime }}\right) \) , then there is a surgery at some time \( \widetilde{\widetilde{t}} \in  \left\lbrack  {-b - \frac{1}{50}{\eta }^{-1}, - b + {\epsilon }^{\prime }}\right\rbrack \) such that \( y \) lies in the instant gluing cap.
