for all sufficiently large \( k \) . By Lemma 5.3.7, we deduce that there exists an isometry \( I \) of \( \mathcal{H} \) to \( \widetilde{\mathcal{H}} \) , and then \( \left( {M,{g}_{ij}\left( \omega \right) ,{F}_{k}\left( \omega \right) \left( P\right) }\right) \) (on compact subsets) is very close to \( \left( {\mathcal{H},{h}_{ij}, P}\right) \) as long as \( \delta \) small enough and \( k \) large enough. Since \( {F}_{k}\left( \omega \right) \left( {\partial {\mathcal{H}}_{a}}\right) \) is strictly concave and the foliation of a neighborhood of \( {F}_{k}\left( \omega \right) \left( {\partial {\mathcal{H}}_{a}}\right) \) by constant mean curvature hypersurfaces has the area as a function with nonzero gradient, by the implicit function theorem, there exists a unique constant mean curvature hypersurface with the same area \( a \) near \( {F}_{k}\left( \omega \right) \left( {\partial {\mathcal{H}}_{a}}\right) \) in \( M \) with the metric \( {g}_{ij}\left( t\right) \) for \( t \) close to \( \omega \) . Hence, when \( k \) sufficiently large, \( {F}_{k}\left( \omega \right) \) can be extended forward in time a little. This is a contradiction and we have proved claim (5.3.9).

We further claim that there must be some \( k \) such that \( {\omega }_{k} =  + \infty \) (i.e., we can smoothly continue the family of harmonic diffeomorphisms \( {F}_{k}\left( t\right) \) for all \( {t}_{k} \leq  t <  + \infty \) , in other words, there must be at least one hyperbolic piece persisting). We argue by contradiction. Suppose for each \( k \) large enough, we can continue the family \( {F}_{k}\left( t\right) \) for \( {t}_{k} \leq  t \leq  {\omega }_{k} <  + \infty \) with

\[
{\begin{Vmatrix}{F}_{k}^{ * }\left( {\omega }_{k}\right) {g}_{ij}\left( {\omega }_{k}\right)  - {h}_{ij}\end{Vmatrix}}_{{C}^{q}\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{a}\right) } = \delta .
\]

Then as before, we consider the new sequence of the manifolds \( M \) with metrics \( {g}_{ij}\left( {\omega }_{k}\right) \) and origins \( {F}_{k}\left( {\omega }_{k}\right) \left( P\right) \) . For sufficiently large \( k \) , we can obtain diffeomorphisms \( {\widetilde{F}}_{k} \) of neighborhoods of \( {\widetilde{B}}_{k} \) into \( M \) with \( {\widetilde{F}}_{k}\left( \widetilde{P}\right)  = {F}_{k}\left( {\omega }_{k}\right) \left( P\right) \) which are as close to preserving the metric as we like, where \( {\widetilde{B}}_{k} \) is a sequence of compact sets, exhausting some hyperbolic three-manifold \( \mathcal{H} \) , of finite volume and with no fewer cusps (than \( \mathcal{H} \) ), and containing \( \widetilde{P} \) ; moreover, the set \( {\widetilde{F}}_{k}\left( {\widetilde{B}}_{k}\right) \) will contain all the points out to any fixed distance we need from the point \( {F}_{k}\left( {\omega }_{k}\right) \left( P\right) \) ; and hence

\[
{\widetilde{F}}_{k}\left( {\widetilde{B}}_{k}\right)  \supseteq  {F}_{k}\left( {\omega }_{k}\right) \left( {\mathcal{H}}_{a}\right)
\]

since \( {\mathcal{H}}_{a} \) is at bounded distance from \( P \) and \( {F}_{k}\left( {\omega }_{k}\right) \) is reasonably close to preserving the metrics. Then we can form the composition

\[
{G}_{k} = {\widetilde{F}}_{k}^{-1} \circ  {F}_{k}\left( {\omega }_{k}\right)  : \;{\mathcal{H}}_{a} \rightarrow  \widetilde{\mathcal{H}}.
\]

Since the \( {\widetilde{F}}_{k} \) are as close to preserving the metric as we like, for any \( \widetilde{\delta } > \delta \) we have

\[
{\begin{Vmatrix}{G}_{k}^{ * }{\widetilde{h}}_{ij} - {h}_{ij}\end{Vmatrix}}_{{C}^{q}\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{a}\right) } < \widetilde{\delta }
\]

for large enough \( k \) . Then a subsequence of \( {G}_{k} \) converges at least in \( {C}^{q - 1}\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{a}\right) \) topology to a map \( {G}_{\infty } \) of \( {\mathcal{H}}_{a} \) into \( \widetilde{\mathcal{H}} \) . By the same reason as in the argument of previous two paragraphs, the limit map \( {G}_{\infty } \) is a smooth harmonic diffeomorphism from \( {\mathcal{H}}_{a} \) into \( \widetilde{\mathcal{H}} \) with the metric \( {\widetilde{h}}_{ij} \) , and takes \( \partial {\mathcal{H}}_{a} \) to a constant mean curvature hypersurface \( {G}_{\infty }\left( {\partial {\mathcal{H}}_{a}}\right) \) of \( \left( {\widetilde{\mathcal{H}},{\widetilde{h}}_{ij}}\right) \) with the area \( a \) , and also satisfies the free boundary condition. Moreover we still have

(5.3.11)

\[
{\begin{Vmatrix}{G}_{\infty }^{ * }{\widetilde{h}}_{ij} - {h}_{ij}\end{Vmatrix}}_{{C}^{q}\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{a}\right) } = \delta .
\]

Now by Lemma 5.3.7 we deduce that there exists an isometry \( I \) of \( \mathcal{H} \) to \( \widetilde{\mathcal{H}} \) with

\[
{d}_{{C}^{{l}_{0}}\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{a}\right) }\left( {{G}_{\infty }, I}\right)  < {\varepsilon }_{0}.
\]

By using \( I \) to identify \( {\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}}_{a} \) and \( {\mathcal{H}}_{a} \) , we see that the map \( {I}^{-1} \circ  {G}_{\infty } \) is a harmonic diffeomorphism of \( {\mathcal{H}}_{a} \) to itself which satisfies the free boundary condition and

\[
{d}_{{C}^{{l}_{0}}\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{a}\right) }\left( {{I}^{-1} \circ  {G}_{\infty },{Id}}\right)  < {\varepsilon }_{0}.
\]

From the uniqueness in Lemma 5.3.8 we conclude that \( {I}^{-1} \circ  {G}_{\infty } = {Id} \) which contradicts with (5.3.11). This shows at least one hyperbolic piece persists. Moreover the pull-back of the solution metric \( {g}_{ij}\left( t\right) \) by \( {F}_{k}\left( t\right) \) , for \( {t}_{k} \leq  t <  + \infty \) , is as close to the hyperbolic metric \( {h}_{ij} \) as we like.

We can continue to form other persistent hyperbolic pieces in the same way as long as there are any points \( {P}_{k} \) outside of the chosen pieces where the injectivity radius at times \( {t}_{k} \rightarrow  \infty \) are all at least some fixed positive number \( \rho  > 0 \) . The only modification in the proof is to take the new limit \( \mathcal{H} \) to have the least possible number of cusps out of all remaining possible limits.

Note that the volume of the normalized Ricci flow is constant in time. Therefore by combining with Margulis lemma (see for example [55] [76]), we have proved that there exists a finite collection of complete noncompact hyperbolic three-manifolds \( {\mathcal{H}}_{1},\ldots ,{\mathcal{H}}_{m} \) with finite volume, a small number \( a > 0 \) and a time \( T <  + \infty \) such that for all \( t \) beyond \( T \) we can find diffeomorphisms \( {\varphi }_{l}\left( t\right) \) of \( {\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{l}\right) }_{a} \) into \( M,1 \leq  l \leq  m \) , so that the pull-back of the solution metric \( {g}_{ij}\left( t\right) \) by \( {\varphi }_{l}\left( t\right) \) is as close to the hyperbolic metrics as we like and the exceptional part of \( M \) where the points are not in the image of any \( {\varphi }_{l} \) has the injectivity radii everywhere as small as we like.

## Part III: Incompressibility

We remain to show that the boundary tori of any persistent hyperbolic piece are incompressible, in the sense that the fundamental group of the torus injects into that of the whole manifold. The argument of this part is a parabolic version of Schoen and Yau's minimal surface argument in [109, 110, 111].

Let \( B \) be a small positive number and assume the above positive number \( a \) is much smaller than \( B \) . Denote by \( {M}_{a} \) a persistent hyperbolic piece of the manifold \( M \) truncated by boundary tori of area \( a \) with constant mean curvature and denote by \( {M}_{a}^{c} = M \smallsetminus  {\overset{ \circ  }{M}}_{a} \) the part of \( M \) exterior to \( {M}_{a} \) . Thus there is a persistent hyperbolic piece \( {M}_{B} \subset  {M}_{a} \) of the manifold \( M \) truncated by boundary tori of area \( B \) with constant mean curvature. We also denote by \( {M}_{B}^{c} = M \smallsetminus  {M}_{B} \) . By Van Kampen’s Theorem, if \( {\pi }_{1}\left( {\partial {M}_{B}}\right) \) injects into \( {\pi }_{1}\left( {M}_{B}^{c}\right) \) then it injects into \( {\pi }_{1}\left( M\right) \) also. Thus we only need to show \( {\pi }_{1}\left( {\partial {M}_{B}}\right) \) injects into \( {\pi }_{1}\left( {M}_{B}^{c}\right) \) .

We will argue by contradiction. Let \( T \) be a torus in \( \partial {M}_{B} \) . Suppose \( {\pi }_{1}\left( T\right) \) does not inject into \( {\pi }_{1}\left( {M}_{B}^{c}\right) \) , then by Dehn’s Lemma the kernel is a cyclic subgroup of \( {\pi }_{1}\left( T\right) \) generated by a primitive element. The work of Meeks-Yau [86] or Meeks-Simon-Yau [87] shows that among all disks in \( {M}_{B}^{c} \) whose boundary curve lies in \( T \) and generates the kernel, there is a smooth embedded disk normal to the boundary which has the least possible area. Let \( A = A\left( t\right) \) be the area of this disk. This is defined for all \( t \) sufficiently large. We will show that \( A\left( t\right) \) decreases at a rate bounded away from zero which will be a contradiction.

Let us compute the rate at which \( A\left( t\right) \) changes under the Ricci flow. We need to show \( A\left( t\right) \) decrease at least at a certain rate, and since \( A\left( t\right) \) is the minimum area to bound any disk in the given homotopy class, it suffices to find some such disk whose area decreases at least that fast. We choose this disk as follows. Pick the minimal disk at time \( {t}_{0} \) , and extend it smoothly a little past the boundary torus since the minimal disk is normal to the boundary. For times \( t \) a little bigger than \( {t}_{0} \) , the boundary torus may need to move a little to stay constant mean curvature with area \( B \) as the metrics change, but we leave the surface alone and take the bounding disk to be the one cut off from it by the new torus. The change of the area \( \widetilde{A}\left( t\right) \) of such disk comes from the change in the metric and the change in the boundary.

For the change in the metric, we choose an orthonormal frame \( X, Y, Z \) at a point \( x \) in the disk so that \( X \) and \( Y \) are tangent to the disk while \( Z \) is normal and compute the rate of change of the area element \( {d\sigma } \) on the disk as

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{d\sigma } = \frac{1}{2}{\left( {g}^{ij}\right) }^{T}\left( {\frac{2}{3}r{\left( {g}_{ij}\right) }^{T} - 2{\left( {R}_{ij}\right) }^{T}}\right) {d\sigma }
\]

\[
= \left\lbrack  {\frac{2}{3}r - \operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, X}\right)  - \operatorname{Ric}\left( {Y, Y}\right) }\right\rbrack  {d\sigma },
\]

since the metric evolves by the normalized Ricci flow. Here \( {\left( \cdot \right) }^{T} \) denotes the tangential projections on the disk. Notice the torus \( T \) may move in time to preserve constant mean curvature and constant area \( B \) . Suppose the boundary of the disk evolves with a normal velocity \( N \) . The change of the area at boundary along a piece of length \( {ds} \) is given by \( {Nds} \) . Thus the total change of the area \( \widetilde{A}\left( t\right) \) is given by

\[
\frac{d\widetilde{A}}{dt} = \iint \left( {\frac{2}{3}r - \operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, X}\right)  - \operatorname{Ric}\left( {Y, Y}\right) }\right) {d\sigma } + {\int }_{\partial }{Nds}.
\]

Note that

\[
\operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, X}\right)  + \operatorname{Ric}\left( {Y, Y}\right)  = R\left( {X, Y, X, Y}\right)  + R\left( {X, Z, X, Z}\right)
\]

\[
+ R\left( {Y, X, Y, X}\right)  + R\left( {Y, Z, Y, Z}\right)
\]

\[
= \frac{1}{2}R + R\left( {X, Y, X, Y}\right) .
\]

By the Gauss equation, the Gauss curvature \( K \) of the disk is given by

\[
K = R\left( {X, Y, X, Y}\right)  + \det {II}
\]

where \( {II} \) is the second fundamental form of the disk in \( {M}_{B}^{c} \) . This gives at \( t = {t}_{0} \) ,

\[
\frac{dA}{dt} \leq  \iint \left( {\frac{2}{3}r - \frac{1}{2}R}\right) {d\sigma } - \iint \left( {K - \det {II}}\right) {d\sigma } + {\int }_{\partial }{Nds}
\]

Since the bounding disk is a minimal surface, we have

\[
\det {II} \leq  0\text{ . }
\]

The Gauss-Bonnet Theorem tells us that for a disk

\[
\int \int {Kd\sigma } + {\int }_{\partial }{kds} = {2\pi }
\]

where \( k \) is the geodesic curvature of the boundary. Thus we obtain

(5.3.12)

\[
\frac{dA}{dt} \leq  \iint \left( {\frac{2}{3}r - \frac{1}{2}R}\right) {d\sigma } + {\int }_{\partial }{kds} + {\int }_{\partial }{Nds} - {2\pi }.
\]

Recall that we are assuming \( {R}_{\min }\left( t\right) \) increases monotonically to -6 as \( t \rightarrow   + \infty \) . By the evolution equation of the scalar curvature,

\[
\frac{d}{dt}{R}_{\min }\left( t\right)  \geq  4\left( {r\left( t\right)  - {R}_{\min }\left( t\right) }\right)
\]

and then

\[
{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\left( {r\left( t\right)  - {R}_{\min }\left( t\right) }\right) {dt} <  + \infty .
\]

This implies that \( r\left( t\right)  \rightarrow   - 6 \) as \( t \rightarrow   + \infty \) by using the derivatives estimate for the curvatures. Thus for every \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) we have

\[
\frac{2}{3}r - \frac{1}{2}R \leq   - \left( {1 - \varepsilon }\right)
\]

for \( t \) sufficiently large. And then the first term on RHS of (5.3.12) is bounded above by

\[
\iint \left( {\frac{2}{3}r - \frac{1}{2}R}\right) {d\sigma } \leq   - \left( {1 - \varepsilon }\right) A.
\]

The geodesic curvature \( k \) of the boundary of the minimal disk is the acceleration of a curve moving with unit speed along the intersection of the disk with the torus; since the disk and torus are normal, this is the same as the second fundamental form of the torus in the direction of the curve of intersection. Now if the metric were actually hyperbolic, the second fundamental form of the torus would be exactly 1 in all directions. Note that the persistent hyperbolic pieces are as close to the standard hyperbolic as we like. This makes that the second term of RHS of (5.3.12) is bounded above by

\[
{\int }_{\partial }{kds} \leq  \left( {1 + {\varepsilon }_{0}}\right) L
\]

for some sufficiently small positive number \( {\varepsilon }_{0} > 0 \) , where \( L \) is the length of the boundary curve. Also since the metric on the persistent hyperbolic pieces are close to the standard hyperbolic as we like, its change under the normalized Ricci flow is as small as we like; So the motion of the constant mean curvature torus of fixed area \( B \) will have a normal velocity \( N \) as small as we like. This again makes the third term of RHS of (5.3.12) bounded above by

\[
{\int }_{\partial }{Nds} \leq  {\varepsilon }_{0}L
\]

Combining these estimates, we obtain

(5.3.13)

\[
\frac{dA}{dt} \leq  \left( {1 + 2{\varepsilon }_{0}}\right) L - \left( {1 - {\varepsilon }_{0}}\right) A - {2\pi }
\]

on the persistent hyperbolic piece, where \( {\varepsilon }_{0} \) is some sufficiently small positive number.

We next need to bound the length \( L \) in terms of the area \( A \) . Since \( a \) is much smaller than \( B \) , for large \( t \) the metric is as close as we like to the standard hyperbolic one; not just on the persistent hyperbolic piece \( {M}_{B} \) but as far beyond as we like. Thus for a long distance into \( {M}_{B}^{c} \) the metric will look nearly like a standard hyperbolic cusplike collar.

Let us first recall a special coordinate system on the standard hyperbolic cusp projecting beyond torus \( {T}_{1} \) in \( \partial {\mathcal{H}}_{1} \) as follows. The universal cover of the flat torus \( {T}_{1} \) can be mapped conformally to the \( x - y \) plane so that the deck transformation of \( {T}_{1} \) become translations in \( x \) and \( y \) , and so that the Euclidean area of the quotient is 1 ; then these coordinates are unique up to a translation. The hyperbolic cusp projecting beyond the torus \( {T}_{1} \) in \( \partial {\mathcal{H}}_{1} \) can be parametrized by \( \left\{  {\left( {x, y, z}\right)  \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{3} \mid  z > 0}\right\} \) with the hyperbolic metric

(5.3.14)

\[
d{s}^{2} = \frac{d{x}^{2} + d{y}^{2} + d{z}^{2}}{{z}^{2}}.
\]

Note that we can make the solution metric, in an arbitrarily large neighborhood of the torus \( T \) (of \( \partial {M}_{B} \) ), as close to hyperbolic as we wish (in the sense that there exists a diffeomorphism from a large neighborhood of the torus \( {T}_{B} \) (of \( \partial {\mathcal{H}}_{B} \) ) on the standard hyperbolic cusp to the above neighborhood of the torus \( T \) (of \( \partial {M}_{B} \) ) such that the pull-back of the solution metric by the diffeomorphism is as close to the hyperbolic metric as we wish). Then by using this diffeomorphism (up to a slight modification) we can parametrize the cusplike tube of \( {M}_{B}^{c} \) projecting beyond the torus \( T \) in \( \partial {M}_{B} \) by \( \{ \left( {x, y, z}\right)  \mid  z \geq  \zeta \} \) where the height \( \zeta \) is chosen so that the torus in the hyperbolic cusp at height \( \zeta \) has the area \( B \) .

Now consider our minimal disk, and let \( L\left( z\right) \) be the length of the curve of the intersection of the disk with the torus at height \( z \) in the above coordinate system, and also let \( A\left( z\right) \) be the area of the part of the disk between \( \zeta \) and \( z \) . We now want to derive a monotonicity formula on the area \( A\left( z\right) \) for the minimal surface.

For almost every \( z \) the intersection of the disk with the torus at height \( z \) is a smooth embedded curve or a finite union of them by the standard transversality theorem. If there is more than one curve, at least one of them is not homotopic to a point in \( T \) and represents the primitive generator in the kernel of \( {\pi }_{1}\left( T\right) \) such that a part of the original disk beyond height \( z \) continues to a disk that bounds it. We extend this disk back to the initial height \( \zeta \) by dropping the curve straight down. Let \( \widetilde{L}\left( z\right) \) be the length of the curve we picked at height \( z \) ; of course \( \widetilde{L}\left( z\right)  \leq  L\left( z\right) \) with equality if it is the only piece. Let \( \widetilde{L}\left( w\right) \) denote the length of the same curve in the \( x - y \) plane dropped down to height \( w \) for \( \zeta  \leq  w \leq  z \) . In the hyperbolic space we would have

\[
\widetilde{L}\left( w\right)  = \frac{z}{w}\widetilde{L}\left( z\right)
\]

exactly. In our case there is a small error proportional to \( \widetilde{L}\left( z\right) \) and we can also take it proportional to the distance \( z - w \) by which it drops since \( {\left. \widetilde{L}\left( w\right) \right| }_{w = z} = \widetilde{L}\left( z\right) \) and the solution metric is close to the hyperbolic in the \( {C}_{loc}^{\infty } \) topology. Thus, for arbitrarily given \( \delta  > 0 \) and \( {\zeta }^{ * } > \zeta \) , as the solution metric is sufficiently close to hyperbolic, we have

\[
\left| {\widetilde{L}\left( w\right)  - \frac{z}{w}\widetilde{L}\left( z\right) }\right|  \leq  \delta \left( {z - w}\right) \widetilde{L}\left( z\right)
\]

for all \( z \) and \( w \) in \( \zeta  \leq  w \leq  z \leq  {\zeta }^{ * } \) . Now given \( \varepsilon \) and \( {\zeta }^{ * } \) pick \( \delta  = {2\varepsilon }/{\zeta }^{ * } \) . Then

(5.3.15)

\[
\widetilde{L}\left( w\right)  \leq  \frac{z}{w}\widetilde{L}\left( z\right) \left\lbrack  {1 + \frac{{2\varepsilon }\left( {z - w}\right) }{w}}\right\rbrack  .
\]

When we drop the curve vertically for the construction of the new disk we get an area \( \widetilde{A}\left( z\right) \) between \( \zeta \) and \( z \) given by

\[
\widetilde{A}\left( z\right)  = \left( {1 + o\left( 1\right) }\right) {\int }_{\zeta }^{z}\frac{\widetilde{L}\left( w\right) }{w}{dw}.
\]

Here and in the following \( o\left( 1\right) \) denotes various small error quantities as the solution metric close to hyperbolic. On the other hand if we do not drop vertically we pick up even more area, so the area \( A\left( z\right) \) of the original disk between \( \zeta \) and \( z \) has

(5.3.16)

\[
A\left( z\right)  \geq  \left( {1 - o\left( 1\right) }\right) {\int }_{\zeta }^{z}\frac{L\left( w\right) }{w}{dw}.
\]

Since the original disk minimized among all disks bounded a curve in the primitive generator of the kernel of \( {\pi }_{1}\left( T\right) \) , and the new disk beyond the height \( z \) is part of the original disk, we have

\[
A\left( z\right)  \leq  \widetilde{A}\left( z\right)
\]

and then by combining with (5.3.15),

\[
{\int }_{\zeta }^{z}\frac{L\left( w\right) }{w}{dw} \leq  \left( {1 + o\left( 1\right) }\right) z\widetilde{L}\left( z\right) {\int }_{\zeta }^{z}\left\lbrack  {\frac{1 - {2\varepsilon }}{{w}^{2}} + \frac{2\varepsilon z}{{w}^{3}}}\right\rbrack  {dw}
\]

\[
\leq  \left( {1 + o\left( 1\right) }\right) L\left( z\right) \frac{\left( z - \zeta \right) }{\zeta }\left\lbrack  {1 + \varepsilon \left( \frac{z - \zeta }{\zeta }\right) }\right\rbrack  .
\]

Here we used the fact that \( \widetilde{L}\left( z\right)  \leq  L\left( z\right) \) . Since the solution metric is sufficiently close to hyperbolic, we have

\[
\frac{d}{dz}\left( {{\int }_{\zeta }^{z}\frac{L\left( w\right) }{w}{dw}}\right)  = \frac{L\left( z\right) }{z}
\]

\[
\geq  \left( {1 - o\left( 1\right) }\right) \frac{\zeta }{z\left( {z - \zeta }\right) }\left\lbrack  {1 - \varepsilon \left( \frac{z - \zeta }{\zeta }\right) }\right\rbrack  {\int }_{\zeta }^{z}\frac{L\left( w\right) }{w}{dw}
\]

\[
\geq  \left\lbrack  {\frac{1}{z - \zeta } - \frac{1 + {2\varepsilon }}{z}}\right\rbrack  {\int }_{\zeta }^{z}\frac{L\left( w\right) }{w}{dw}
\]

or equivalently

(5.3.17)

\[
\frac{d}{dz}\log \left\{  {\frac{{z}^{1 + {2\varepsilon }}}{\left( z - \zeta \right) }{\int }_{\zeta }^{z}\frac{L\left( w\right) }{w}{dw}}\right\}   \geq  0.
\]

This is the desired monotonicity formula for the area \( A\left( z\right) \) .

It follows directly from (5.3.16) and (5.3.17) that

\[
\frac{{z}^{1 + {2\varepsilon }}}{\left( z - \zeta \right) }A\left( z\right)  \geq  \left( {1 - o\left( 1\right) }\right) {\zeta }^{2\varepsilon }L\left( \zeta \right)
\]

or equivalently

\[
L\left( \zeta \right)  \leq  \left( {1 + o\left( 1\right) }\right) {\left( \frac{z}{\zeta }\right) }^{2\varepsilon }\frac{z}{z - \zeta }A\left( z\right)
\]

for all \( z \in  \left\lbrack  {\zeta ,{\zeta }^{ * }}\right\rbrack \) . Since the solution metric, in an arbitrarily large neighborhood of the torus \( T \) (of \( \partial {M}_{B} \) ), as close to hyperbolic as we wish, we may assume that \( {\zeta }^{ * } \) is so large that \( \sqrt{{\zeta }^{ * }} > \zeta \) and \( \frac{\sqrt{{\zeta }^{ * }}}{\sqrt{{\zeta }^{ * }} - \zeta } \) is close to 1, and also \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) is so small that \( {\left( \frac{\sqrt{{\zeta }^{ * }}}{\zeta }\right) }^{2\varepsilon } \) is close to 1 . Thus for arbitrarily small \( {\delta }_{0} > 0 \) , we have

(5.3.18)

\[
L\left( \zeta \right)  \leq  \left( {1 + {\delta }_{0}}\right) A\left( \sqrt{{\zeta }^{ * }}\right) .
\]

Now recall that (5.3.13) states

\[
\frac{dA}{dt} \leq  \left( {1 + 2{\varepsilon }_{0}}\right) L - \left( {1 - {\varepsilon }_{0}}\right) A - {2\pi }.
\]

We now claim that if

\[
\left( {1 + 2{\varepsilon }_{0}}\right) L - \left( {1 - {\varepsilon }_{0}}\right) A \geq  0
\]

then \( L = L\left( \zeta \right) \) is uniformly bounded from above.

Indeed by the assumption we have

\[
A\left( {\zeta }^{ * }\right)  \leq  \frac{\left( 1 + 2{\varepsilon }_{0}\right) }{\left( 1 - {\varepsilon }_{0}\right) }L\left( \zeta \right)
\]

since \( A\left( {\zeta }^{ * }\right)  \leq  A \) . By combining with (5.3.16) we have some \( {z}_{0} \in  \left( {\sqrt{{\zeta }^{ * }},{\zeta }^{ * }}\right) \) satisfying

\[
\frac{L\left( {z}_{0}\right) }{{z}_{0}}\left( {{\zeta }^{ * } - \sqrt{{\zeta }^{ * }}}\right)  \leq  {\int }_{\sqrt{{\zeta }^{ * }}}^{{\zeta }^{ * }}\frac{L\left( w\right) }{w}{dw}
\]

\[
\leq  \left( {1 + o\left( 1\right) }\right) A\left( {\zeta }^{ * }\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \left( {1 + o\left( 1\right) }\right) \left( \frac{1 + 2{\varepsilon }_{0}}{1 - {\varepsilon }_{0}}\right) L\left( \zeta \right) .
\]

Thus for \( {\zeta }^{ * } \) suitably large, by noting that the solution metric on a large neighborhood of \( T \) (of \( \partial {M}_{B} \) ) is sufficiently close to hyperbolic, we have

(5.3.19)

\[
L\left( {z}_{0}\right)  \leq  \left( {1 + 4{\varepsilon }_{0}}\right) \frac{{z}_{0}}{{\zeta }^{ * }}L\left( \zeta \right)
\]

for some \( {z}_{0} \in  \left( {\sqrt{{\zeta }^{ * }},{\zeta }^{ * }}\right) \) . It is clear that we may assume the intersection curve between the minimal disk with the torus at this height \( {z}_{0} \) is smooth and embedded. If the intersection curve at the height \( {z}_{0} \) has more than one piece, as before one of them will represent the primitive generator in the kernel of \( {\pi }_{1}\left( T\right) \) , and we can ignore the others. Let us move (the piece of) the intersection curve on the torus at height \( {z}_{0} \) through as small as possible area in the same homotopy class of \( {\pi }_{1}\left( T\right) \) to a curve which is a geodesic circle in the flat torus coming from our special coordinates, and then drop this geodesic circle vertically in the special coordinates to obtain another new disk. We will compare the area of this new disk with the original minimal disk as follows.

Denote by \( G \) the length of the geodesic circle in the standard hyperbolic cusp at height 1 . Then the length of the geodesic circle at height \( {z}_{0} \) will be \( G/{z}_{0} \) . Observe that given an embedded curve of length \( l \) circling the cylinder \( {S}^{1} \times  \mathbb{R} \) of circumference \( w \) once, it is possible to deform the curve through an area not bigger than \( {lw} \) into a meridian circle. Note that (the piece of) the intersection curve represents the primitive generator in the kernel of \( {\pi }_{1}\left( T\right) \) . Note also that the solution metric is sufficiently close to the hyperbolic metric. Then the area of the deformation from (the piece of) the intersection curve on the torus at height \( {z}_{0} \) to the geodesic circle at height \( {z}_{0} \) is bounded by

\[
\left( {1 + o\left( 1\right) }\right) \left( \frac{G}{{z}_{0}}\right)  \cdot  L\left( {z}_{0}\right) .
\]

The area to drop the geodesic circle from height \( {z}_{0} \) to height \( \zeta \) is bounded by

\[
\left( {1 + o\left( 1\right) }\right) {\int }_{\zeta }^{{z}_{0}}\frac{G}{{w}^{2}}{dw}.
\]

Hence comparing the area of the original minimal disk to that of this new disk gives

\[
A\left( {z}_{0}\right)  \leq  \left( {1 + o\left( 1\right) }\right) G\left\lbrack  {\frac{L\left( {z}_{0}\right) }{{z}_{0}} + \left( {\frac{1}{\zeta } - \frac{1}{{z}_{0}}}\right) }\right\rbrack  .
\]

By (5.3.18),(5.3.19) and the fact that \( {z}_{0} \in  \left( {\sqrt{{\zeta }^{ * }},{\zeta }^{ * }}\right) \) , this in turn gives

\[
L\left( \zeta \right)  \leq  \left( {1 + {\delta }_{0}}\right) A\left( {z}_{0}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \left( {1 + {\delta }_{0}}\right) G\left\lbrack  {\left( {1 + 4{\varepsilon }_{0}}\right) \frac{L\left( \zeta \right) }{{\zeta }^{ * }} + \frac{1}{\zeta }}\right\rbrack  .
\]

Since \( {\zeta }^{ * } \) is suitably large, we obtain

\[
L\left( \zeta \right)  \leq  {2G}/\zeta
\]

This gives the desired assertion since \( G \) is fixed from the geometry of the limit hyperbolic manifold \( \mathcal{H} \) and \( \zeta \) is very large as long as the area \( B \) of \( \partial {M}_{B} \) small enough.

Thus the combination of (5.3.13), (5.3.18) and the assertion implies that either

\[
\frac{d}{dt}A \leq   - {2\pi }
\]

\[
\frac{d}{dt}A \leq  \left( {1 + 2{\varepsilon }_{0}}\right) L - \left( {1 - {\varepsilon }_{0}}\right) A - {2\pi }
\]

\[
\leq  \left( {1 + 2{\varepsilon }_{0}}\right) \frac{2G}{\zeta } - {2\pi }
\]

\[
\leq   - \pi
\]

since the solution metric on a very large neighborhood of the torus \( T \) (of \( \partial {M}_{B} \) ) is sufficiently close to hyperbolic and \( \zeta \) is very large as the area \( B \) of \( \partial {M}_{B} \) small enough. This is impossible because \( A \geq  0 \) and the persistent hyperbolic pieces go on forever. The contradiction shows that \( {\pi }_{1}\left( T\right) \) in fact injects into \( {\pi }_{1}\left( {M}_{B}^{c}\right) \) . This proves that \( {\pi }_{1}\left( {\partial {M}_{B}}\right) \) injects into \( {\pi }_{1}\left( M\right) \) .

Therefore we have completed the proof of Theorem 5.3.4. [

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \( {g}_{ij} \) be a complete Riemannian metric on \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\left( {n \geq  3}\right) \) with nonnegative curvature operator and positive scalar curvature which is asymptotic to a round cylinder of scalar curvature 1 at infinity. Then there is a complete solution \( {g}_{ij}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) to the Ricci flow, with \( {g}_{ij} \) as initial metric, which exists on the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {0,\frac{n - 1}{2}}\right) \) , has bounded curvature at each time \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,\frac{n - 1}{2}}\right) \) , and satisfies the estimate

\[
R\left( {x, t}\right)  \geq  \frac{{C}^{-1}}{\frac{n - 1}{2} - t}
\]

for some \( C \) depending only on the initial metric \( {g}_{ij} \) .

Since the initial metric has bounded curvature operator and a positive lower bound on its scalar curvature, the Ricci flow has a solution \( {g}_{ij}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) defined on a maximal time interval \( \lbrack 0, T) \) with \( T < \infty \) which has bounded curvature on \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \times  \left\lbrack  {0,{T}^{\prime }}\right\rbrack \) for each \( 0 < {T}^{\prime } < T \) . By Proposition 2.1.4, the solution \( {g}_{ij}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) has nonnegative curvature operator for all \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) . Note that the injectivity radius of the initial metric has a positive lower bound. As we remarked at the beginning of Section 3.4, the same proof of Perelman's no local collapsing theorem I concludes that \( {g}_{ij}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) is \( \kappa \) -noncollapsed on all scales less than \( \sqrt{T} \) for some \( \kappa  > 0 \) depending only on the initial metric.

We will first prove the following assertion.

CLAIM 1. There is a positive function \( \omega  : \lbrack 0,\infty ) \rightarrow  \lbrack 0,\infty ) \) depending only on the initial metric and \( \kappa \) such that

\[
R\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  R\left( {y, t}\right) \omega \left( {R\left( {y, t}\right) {d}_{t}^{2}\left( {x, y}\right) }\right)
\]

for all \( x, y \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n}, t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) .

The proof is similar to that of Theorem 6.4.3. Notice that the initial metric has nonnegative curvature operator and its scalar curvature satisfies the bounds

(7.3.5)

\[
{C}^{-1} \leq  R\left( x\right)  \leq  C
\]

for some positive constant \( C \) . By the maximum principle, we know \( T \geq  \frac{1}{2nC} \) and \( R\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {2C} \) for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,\frac{1}{4nC}}\right\rbrack \) . The assertion is clearly true for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,\frac{1}{4nC}}\right\rbrack \) .

Now fix \( \left( {y,{t}_{0}}\right)  \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \times  \lbrack 0, T) \) with \( {t}_{0} \geq  \frac{1}{4nC} \) . Let \( z \) be the closest point to \( y \) with the property \( R\left( {z,{t}_{0}}\right) {d}_{{t}_{0}}^{2}\left( {z, y}\right)  = 1 \) (at time \( {t}_{0} \) ). Draw a shortest geodesic from \( y \) to \( z \) and choose a point \( \widetilde{z} \) on the geodesic satisfying \( {d}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {z,\widetilde{z}}\right)  = \frac{1}{4}R{\left( z,{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}} \) , then we have

\[
R\left( {x,{t}_{0}}\right)  \leq  \frac{1}{{\left( \frac{1}{2}R{\left( z,{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right) }^{2}}\;\text{ on }{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {\widetilde{z},\frac{1}{4}R{\left( z,{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) .
\]

Note that \( R\left( {x, t}\right)  \geq  {C}^{-1} \) everywhere by the evolution equation of the scalar curvature. Then by the Li-Yau-Hamilton inequality (Corollary 2.5.5), for all \( \left( {x, t}\right)  \in \; {B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {\widetilde{z},\frac{1}{8nC}R{\left( z,{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0} - {\left( \frac{1}{8nC}R{\left( z,{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right) }^{2},{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) , we have

\[
R\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  \left( \frac{{t}_{0}}{{t}_{0} - {\left( \frac{1}{{8n}\sqrt{C}}\right) }^{2}}\right) \frac{1}{{\left( \frac{1}{2}R{\left( z,{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right) }^{2}}
\]

\[
\leq  {\left\lbrack  \frac{1}{8nC}R{\left( z,{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right\rbrack  }^{-2}.
\]

Combining this with the \( \kappa \) -noncollapsing property, we have

\[
\operatorname{Vol}\left( {{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {\widetilde{z},\frac{1}{8nC}R{\left( z,{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) }\right)  \geq  \kappa {\left( \frac{1}{8nC}R{\left( z,{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right) }^{n}
\]

and then

\[
\operatorname{Vol}\left( {{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {z,{8R}{\left( z,{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) }\right)  \geq  \kappa {\left( \frac{1}{64nC}\right) }^{n}{\left( 8R{\left( z,{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right) }^{n}.
\]

So by Theorem 6.3.3 (ii), we have

\[
R\left( {x,{t}_{0}}\right)  \leq  C\left( \kappa \right) R\left( {z,{t}_{0}}\right) \;\text{ for all }x \in  {B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {z,{4R}{\left( z,{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) .
\]

Here and in the following we denote by \( C\left( \kappa \right) \) various positive constants depending only on \( \kappa , n \) and the initial metric.

Now by the Li-Yau-Hamilton inequality (Corollary 2.5.5) and local gradient estimate of Shi (Theorem 1.4.2), we obtain

\[
R\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  C\left( \kappa \right) R\left( {z,{t}_{0}}\right) \text{ and }\left| {\frac{\partial }{\partial t}R}\right| \left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  C\left( \kappa \right) {\left( R\left( z,{t}_{0}\right) \right) }^{2}
\]

for all \( \left. {\left( {x, t}\right)  \in  {B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {z,{2R}{\left( z,{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) }\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0} - {\left( \frac{1}{8nC}R{\left( z,{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right) }^{2},{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) . Therefore by combining with the Harnack estimate (Corollary 2.5.7), we obtain

\[
R\left( {y,{t}_{0}}\right)  \geq  C{\left( \kappa \right) }^{-1}R\left( {z,{t}_{0} - C{\left( \kappa \right) }^{-1}R{\left( z,{t}_{0}\right) }^{-1}}\right)
\]

\[
\geq  C{\left( \kappa \right) }^{-2}R\left( {z,{t}_{0}}\right)
\]

Consequently, we have showed that there is a constant \( C\left( \kappa \right) \) such that

\[
\operatorname{Vol}\left( {{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {y, R{\left( y,{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) }\right)  \geq  C{\left( \kappa \right) }^{-1}{\left( R{\left( y,{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right) }^{n}
\]

and

\[
R\left( {x,{t}_{0}}\right)  \leq  C\left( \kappa \right) R\left( {y,{t}_{0}}\right) \;\text{ for all }x \in  {B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {y, R{\left( y,{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) .
\]

In general, for any \( r \geq  R{\left( y,{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}} \) , we have

\[
\operatorname{Vol}\left( {{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {y, r}\right) }\right)  \geq  C{\left( \kappa \right) }^{-1}{\left( {r}^{2}R\left( y,{t}_{0}\right) \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{r}^{n}.
\]

By applying Theorem 6.3.3(ii) again, there exists a positive constant \( \omega \left( {{r}^{2}R\left( {y,{t}_{0}}\right) }\right) \) depending only on the constant \( {r}^{2}R\left( {y,{t}_{0}}\right) \) and \( \kappa \) such that

\[
R\left( {x,{t}_{0}}\right)  \leq  R\left( {y,{t}_{0}}\right) \omega \left( {{r}^{2}R\left( {y,{t}_{0}}\right) }\right) \;\text{ for all }x \in  {B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {y,\frac{1}{4}r}\right) .
\]

This proves the desired Claim 1.

Now we study the asymptotic behavior of the solution at infinity. For any \( 0 < \; {t}_{0} < T \) , we know that the metrics \( {g}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) \) with \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) has uniformly bounded curvature. Let \( {x}_{k} \) be a sequence of points with \( {d}_{0}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{k}}\right)  \rightarrow  \infty \) . After passing to a subsequence, \( {g}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) \) around \( {x}_{k} \) will converge to a solution to the Ricci flow on \( \mathbb{R} \times  {\mathbb{S}}^{n - 1} \) with round cylinder metric of scalar curvature 1 as initial data. Denote the limit by \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij} \) . Then by the uniqueness theorem (Theorem 1.2.4), we have

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {x, t}\right)  = \frac{\frac{n - 1}{2}}{\frac{n - 1}{2} - t}\;\text{ for all }t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack  .
\]

It follows that \( T \leq  \frac{n - 1}{2} \) . In order to show \( T = \frac{n - 1}{2} \) , it suffices to prove the following assertion.

CLAIM 2. Suppose \( T < \frac{n - 1}{2} \) . Fix a point \( {x}_{0} \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) , then there is a \( \delta  > 0 \) , such that for any \( x \in  M \) with \( {d}_{0}\left( {x,{x}_{0}}\right)  \geq  {\delta }^{-1} \) , we have

\[
R\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {2C} + \frac{n - 1}{\frac{n - 1}{2} - t}\;\text{ for all }t \in  \lbrack 0, T),
\]

where \( C \) is the constant in (7.3.5).

In view of Claim 1, if Claim 2 holds, then

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{{M}^{n} \times  \lbrack 0, T)}}R\left( {y, t}\right)  \leq  \omega \left( {{\delta }^{-2}\left( {{2C} + \frac{n - 1}{\frac{n - 1}{2} - T}}\right) }\right) \left( {{2C} + \frac{n - 1}{\frac{n - 1}{2} - T}}\right)
\]

\[
< \infty
\]

which will contradict the definition of \( T \) .

To show Claim 2, we argue by contradiction. Suppose for each \( \delta  > 0 \) , there is a point \( \left( {{x}_{\delta },{t}_{\delta }}\right) \) with \( 0 < {t}_{\delta } < T \) such that

\[
R\left( {{x}_{\delta },{t}_{\delta }}\right)  > {2C} + \frac{n - 1}{\frac{n - 1}{2} - {t}_{\delta }}\text{ and }{d}_{0}\left( {{x}_{\delta },{x}_{0}}\right)  \geq  {\delta }^{-1}.
\]

Let

\[
{\bar{t}}_{\delta } = \sup \left\{  {\left. t\right| \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{{M}^{n} \smallsetminus  {B}_{0}\left( {{x}_{0},{\delta }^{-1}}\right) }}R\left( {y, t}\right)  < {2C} + \frac{n - 1}{\frac{n - 1}{2} - t}}\right\}  .
\]

Since \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{{d}_{0}\left( {y,{x}_{0}}\right)  \rightarrow  \infty }}R\left( {y, t}\right)  = \frac{\frac{n - 1}{2}}{\frac{n - 1}{2} - t} \) and \( \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{M \times  \left\lbrack  {0,\frac{1}{4nC}}\right\rbrack  }}R\left( {y, t}\right)  \leq  {2C} \) , we know \( \frac{1}{4nC} \leq  {\bar{t}}_{\delta } \leq \; {t}_{\delta } \) and there is a \( {\bar{x}}_{\delta } \) such that \( {d}_{0}\left( {{x}_{0},{\bar{x}}_{\delta }}\right)  \geq  {\delta }^{-1} \) and \( R\left( {{\bar{x}}_{\delta },{\bar{t}}_{\delta }}\right)  = {2C} + \frac{n - 1}{\frac{n - 1}{2} - {\bar{t}}_{\delta }} \) . By Claim

1 and Hamilton’s compactness theorem (Theorem 4.1.5), for \( \delta  \rightarrow  0 \) and after taking a subsequence, the metrics \( {g}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) \) on \( {B}_{0}\left( {{\bar{x}}_{\delta },\frac{{\delta }^{-1}}{2}}\right) \) over the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {0,{\bar{t}}_{\delta }}\right\rbrack \) will converge to a solution \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij} \) on \( \mathbb{R} \times  {\mathbb{S}}^{n - 1} \) with the standard metric of scalar curvature 1 as initial data over the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {0,{\bar{t}}_{\infty }}\right\rbrack \) , and its scalar curvature satisfies

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {{\bar{x}}_{\infty },{\bar{t}}_{\infty }}\right)  = {2C} + \frac{n - 1}{\frac{n - 1}{2} - {\bar{t}}_{\infty }},
\]

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {2C} + \frac{n - 1}{\frac{n - 1}{2} - {\bar{t}}_{\infty }},\;\text{ for all }t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{\bar{t}}_{\infty }}\right\rbrack  ,
\]

where \( \left( {{\bar{x}}_{\infty },{\bar{t}}_{\infty }}\right) \) is the limit of \( \left( {{\bar{x}}_{\delta },{\bar{t}}_{\delta }}\right) \) . On the other hand, by the uniqueness theorem (Theorem 1.2.4) again, we know

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {{\bar{x}}_{\infty },{\bar{t}}_{\infty }}\right)  = \frac{\frac{n - 1}{2}}{\frac{n - 1}{2} - {\bar{t}}_{\infty }}
\]

which is a contradiction. Hence we have proved Claim 2 and then have verified \( T = \frac{n - 1}{2}. \)

Now we are ready to show

(7.3.6)

\[
R\left( {x, t}\right)  \geq  \frac{{\widetilde{C}}^{-1}}{\frac{n - 1}{2} - t},\;\text{ for all }\left( {x, t}\right)  \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \times  \left\lbrack  {0,\frac{n - 1}{2}}\right) ,
\]

for some positive constant \( \widetilde{C} \) depending only on the initial metric.

For any \( \left( {x, t}\right)  \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \times  \left\lbrack  {0,\frac{n - 1}{2}}\right) \) , by Claim 1 and \( \kappa \) -noncollapsing, there is a constant \( C\left( \kappa \right)  > 0 \) such that

\[
{\operatorname{Vol}}_{t}\left( {{B}_{t}\left( {x, R{\left( x, t\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) }\right)  \geq  C{\left( \kappa \right) }^{-1}{\left( R{\left( x, t\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right) }^{n}.
\]

Then by the well-known volume estimate of Calabi-Yau (see for example [128] or [112]) for complete manifolds with Ric \( \geq  0 \) , for any \( a \geq  1 \) , we have

\[
{\operatorname{Vol}}_{t}\left( {{B}_{t}\left( {x,{aR}{\left( x, t\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) }\right)  \geq  C{\left( \kappa \right) }^{-1}\frac{a}{8n}{\left( R{\left( x, t\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right) }^{n}.
\]

On the other hand, since \( \left( {{\mathbb{R}}^{n},{g}_{ij}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right) \) is asymptotic to a cylinder of scalar curvature \( \left( \frac{n - 1}{2}\right) /\left( {\frac{n - 1}{2} - t}\right) \) , for sufficiently large \( a > 0 \) , we have

\[
{\operatorname{Vol}}_{t}\left( {{B}_{t}\left( {x, a\sqrt{\frac{n - 1}{2} - t}}\right) }\right)  \leq  C\left( n\right) a{\left( \frac{n - 1}{2} - t\right) }^{\frac{n}{2}}.
\]

Combining the two inequalities, for all sufficiently large \( a \) , we have:

\[
C\left( n\right) a{\left( \frac{n - 1}{2} - t\right) }^{\frac{n}{2}} \geq  {\operatorname{Vol}}_{t}\left( {{B}_{t}\left( {x, a\left( \frac{\sqrt{\frac{n - 1}{2} - t}}{R{\left( x, t\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) R{\left( x, t\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\geq  C{\left( \kappa \right) }^{-1}\frac{a}{8n}\left( \frac{\sqrt{\frac{n - 1}{2} - t}}{R{\left( x, t\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) {\left( R{\left( x, t\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right) }^{n},
\]

which gives the desired estimate (7.3.6). Therefore the proof of the proposition is complete. \( \square \)

This formula is obtained from the second Bianchi identity

\[
{\partial }_{i}{R}_{jklm} + {\partial }_{j}{R}_{kilm} + {\partial }_{k}{R}_{ijlm} = 0
\]

by differentiating, exchanging derivatives, permuting indices and contracting. To begin we have

\[
\Delta {R}_{ijkl} = {g}^{pq}{\partial }_{p}{\partial }_{q}{R}_{ijkl} = {g}^{pq}\left( {{\partial }_{p}{\partial }_{i}{R}_{qjkl} - {\partial }_{p}{\partial }_{j}{R}_{qikl}}\right)
\]

by differentiating the second Bianchi identity and contracting. We examine the first term, since the second is symmetric in \( i \) and \( j \) . Interchanging the order of derivatives we have

\[
{g}^{pq}{\partial }_{p}{\partial }_{i}{R}_{qjkl} - {g}^{pq}{\partial }_{i}{\partial }_{p}{R}_{qjkl}
\]

\[
= {g}^{pq}{g}^{mn}\left( {{R}_{piqm}{R}_{njkl} + {R}_{pijm}{R}_{qnkl} + {R}_{pikm}{R}_{qjnl} + {R}_{pilm}{R}_{qjkn}}\right) .
\]

The first of these terms contracts to \( {g}^{pq}{R}_{pjkl}{R}_{qi} \) . On the second term we can use the first Bianchi identity to write it in terms of the tensor \( {B}_{ijkl} \) ; thus

\[
{g}^{pq}{g}^{mn}{R}_{pijm}{R}_{qnkl} =  - {B}_{ijkl} + {B}_{ijlk},
\]

and the last two terms are \( - {B}_{ikjl} + {B}_{iljk} \) . Moreover we have the contracted second Bianchi identity

\[
{g}^{pq}{\partial }_{p}{R}_{qjkl} = {\partial }_{k}{R}_{jl} - {\partial }_{l}{R}_{jk},
\]

to which we apply the derivative \( {\partial }_{i} \) . Then

\[
{g}^{pq}{\partial }_{p}{\partial }_{i}{R}_{qjkl} = {\partial }_{i}{\partial }_{k}{R}_{jl} - {\partial }_{i}{\partial }_{l}{R}_{jk}
\]

\[
- \left( {{B}_{ijkl} - {B}_{ijlk} - {B}_{iljk} + {B}_{ikjl}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {g}^{pq}{R}_{pjkl}{R}_{qi}.
\]

Replacing this in our formula for \( \Delta {R}_{ijkl} \) and doing the same for the term with \( i \) and \( j \) interchanged yields the formula in the lemma.

(Hamilton [58]). Under the Ricci flow (1.1.5), the curvature tensor satisfies the evolution equation

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{R}_{ijkl} = \Delta {R}_{ijkl} + 2\left( {{B}_{ijkl} - {B}_{ijlk} - {B}_{iljk} + {B}_{ikjl}}\right)
\]

\[
- {g}^{pq}\left( {{R}_{pjkl}{R}_{qi} + {R}_{ipkl}{R}_{qj} + {R}_{ijpl}{R}_{qk} + {R}_{ijkp}{R}_{ql}}\right)
\]

where \( {B}_{ijkl} = {g}^{pr}{g}^{qs}{R}_{piqj}{R}_{rksl} \) and \( \Delta \) is the Laplacian with respect to the evolving metric.

Choose \( \left\{  {{x}^{1},\ldots ,{x}^{m}}\right\} \) to be a normal coordinate system at a fixed point. At this point, we compute

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{\Gamma }_{jl}^{h} = \frac{1}{2}{g}^{hm}\left\{  {\frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{j}}\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{g}_{lm}}\right)  + \frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{l}}\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{g}_{jm}}\right)  - \frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{m}}\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{g}_{jl}}\right) }\right\}
\]

\[
= \frac{1}{2}{g}^{hm}\left( {{\nabla }_{j}\left( {-2{R}_{lm}}\right)  + {\nabla }_{l}\left( {-2{R}_{jm}}\right)  - {\nabla }_{m}\left( {-2{R}_{jl}}\right) }\right) ,
\]

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{R}_{ijl}^{h} = \frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{i}}\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{\Gamma }_{jl}^{h}}\right)  - \frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{j}}\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{\Gamma }_{il}^{h}}\right) ,
\]

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{R}_{ijkl} = {g}_{hk}\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{R}_{ijl}^{h} + \frac{\partial {g}_{hk}}{\partial t}{R}_{ijl}^{h}.
\]

Combining these identities we get

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{R}_{ijkl} = {g}_{hk}\left\lbrack  \left( {\frac{1}{2}{\nabla }_{i}\left\lbrack  {{g}^{hm}\left( {{\nabla }_{j}\left( {-2{R}_{lm}}\right)  + {\nabla }_{l}\left( {-2{R}_{jm}}\right)  - {\nabla }_{m}\left( {-2{R}_{jl}}\right) }\right) }\right\rbrack  }\right) \right.
\]

\[
\left. {-\left( {\frac{1}{2}{\nabla }_{j}\left\lbrack  {{g}^{hm}\left( {{\nabla }_{i}\left( {-2{R}_{lm}}\right)  + {\nabla }_{l}\left( {-2{R}_{im}}\right)  - {\nabla }_{m}\left( {-2{R}_{il}}\right) }\right) }\right\rbrack  }\right) }\right\rbrack
\]

\[
- 2{R}_{hk}{R}_{ijl}^{h}
\]

\[
= {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{k}{R}_{jl} - {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{l}{R}_{jk} - {\nabla }_{j}{\nabla }_{k}{R}_{il} + {\nabla }_{j}{\nabla }_{l}{R}_{ik}
\]

\[
- {R}_{ijlp}{g}^{pq}{R}_{qk} - {R}_{ijkp}{g}^{pq}{R}_{ql} - 2{R}_{ijpl}{g}^{pq}{R}_{qk}
\]

\[
= {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{k}{R}_{jl} - {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{l}{R}_{jk} - {\nabla }_{j}{\nabla }_{k}{R}_{il} + {\nabla }_{j}{\nabla }_{l}{R}_{ik}
\]

\[
- {g}^{pq}\left( {{R}_{ijkp}{R}_{ql} + {R}_{ijpl}{R}_{qk}}\right) .
\]

Here we have used the exchanging formula (1.1.3).

Now it remains to check the following identity, which is analogous to the Simon's identity in extrinsic geometry,

(1.3.1)

\[
\Delta {R}_{ijkl} + 2\left( {{B}_{ijkl} - {B}_{ijlk} - {B}_{iljk} + {B}_{ikjl}}\right)
\]

\[
= {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{k}{R}_{jl} - {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{l}{R}_{jk} - {\nabla }_{j}{\nabla }_{k}{R}_{il} + {\nabla }_{j}{\nabla }_{l}{R}_{ik}
\]

\[
+ {g}^{pq}\left( {{R}_{pjkl}{R}_{qi} + {R}_{ipkl}{R}_{qj}}\right) .
\]

Indeed, from the second Bianchi identity (1.1.4), we have

\[
\Delta {R}_{ijkl} = {g}^{pq}{\nabla }_{p}{\nabla }_{q}{R}_{ijkl}
\]

\[
= {g}^{pq}{\nabla }_{p}{\nabla }_{i}{R}_{qjkl} - {g}^{pq}{\nabla }_{p}{\nabla }_{j}{R}_{qikl}.
\]

Let us examine the first term on the RHS. By using the exchanging formula (1.1.3) and the first Bianchi identity (1.1.1), we have

\[
{g}^{pq}{\nabla }_{p}{\nabla }_{i}{R}_{qjkl} - {g}^{pq}{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{p}{R}_{qjkl}
\]

\[
= {g}^{pq}{g}^{mn}\left( {{R}_{piqm}{R}_{njkl} + {R}_{pijm}{R}_{qnkl} + {R}_{pikm}{R}_{qjnl} + {R}_{pilm}{R}_{qjkn}}\right)
\]

\[
= {R}_{im}{g}^{mn}{R}_{njkl} + {g}^{pq}{g}^{mn}{R}_{pimj}\left( {{R}_{qkln} + {R}_{qlnk}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {g}^{pq}{g}^{mn}{R}_{pikm}{R}_{qjnl} + {g}^{pq}{g}^{mn}{R}_{pilm}{R}_{qjkn}
\]

\[
= {R}_{im}{g}^{mn}{R}_{njkl} - {B}_{ijkl} + {B}_{ijlk} - {B}_{ikjl} + {B}_{iljk},
\]

while using the contracted second Bianchi identity

(1.3.2)

\[
{g}^{pq}{\nabla }_{p}{R}_{qjkl} = {\nabla }_{k}{R}_{jl} - {\nabla }_{l}{R}_{jk},
\]

we have

\[
{g}^{pq}{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{p}{R}_{qjkl} = {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{k}{R}_{jl} - {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{l}{R}_{jk}.
\]

Thus

\[
{g}^{pq}{\nabla }_{p}{\nabla }_{i}{R}_{qjkl}
\]

\[
= {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{k}{R}_{jl} - {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{l}{R}_{jk} - \left( {{B}_{ijkl} - {B}_{ijlk} - {B}_{iljk} + {B}_{ikjl}}\right)  + {g}^{pq}{R}_{pjkl}{R}_{qi}.
\]

Therefore we obtain

\[
\Delta {R}_{ijkl}
\]

\[
= {g}^{pq}{\nabla }_{p}{\nabla }_{i}{R}_{qjkl} - {g}^{pq}{\nabla }_{p}{\nabla }_{j}{R}_{qikl}
\]

\[
= {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{k}{R}_{jl} - {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{l}{R}_{jk} - \left( {{B}_{ijkl} - {B}_{ijlk} - {B}_{iljk} + {B}_{ikjl}}\right)  + {g}^{pq}{R}_{pjkl}{R}_{qi}
\]

\[
- {\nabla }_{j}{\nabla }_{k}{R}_{il} + {\nabla }_{j}{\nabla }_{l}{R}_{ik} + \left( {{B}_{jikl} - {B}_{jilk} - {B}_{jlik} + {B}_{jkil}}\right)  - {g}^{pq}{R}_{pikl}{R}_{qj}
\]

\[
= {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{k}{R}_{jl} - {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{l}{R}_{jk} - {\nabla }_{j}{\nabla }_{k}{R}_{il} + {\nabla }_{j}{\nabla }_{l}{R}_{ik}
\]

\[
+ {g}^{pq}\left( {{R}_{pjkl}{R}_{qi} + {R}_{ipkl}{R}_{qj}}\right)  - 2\left( {{B}_{ijkl} - {B}_{ijlk} - {B}_{iljk} + {B}_{ikjl}}\right)
\]

as desired, where in the last step we used the symmetries

(1.3.3)

\[
{B}_{ijkl} = {B}_{klij} = {B}_{jilk}.
\]

knowledge_statements.proof_latex:
This sort of calculation is probably easiest to perform in normal coordinates (or alternatively with respect to an appropriate orthonormal frame) about an arbitrary point \( p \) . The main ingredients are the Bianchi identities. To begin with, we require the second Bianchi identity for the first derivative of Rm,

\[
{\nabla }_{i}{R}_{jkla} + {\nabla }_{j}{R}_{kila} + {\nabla }_{k}{R}_{ijla} = 0.
\]

(Here \( {\nabla }_{i}{R}_{jkla} \mathrel{\text{ := }} \left( {{\nabla }_{\frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{i}}}\operatorname{Rm}}\right) \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{j}},\frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{k}},\frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{l}},\frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{a}}}\right) \) .) Taking one further derivative, tracing, and restricting our attention to the point \( p \) , we find that

\[
\Delta {R}_{jkla} + {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}{R}_{kila} - {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{k}{R}_{jila} = 0. \tag{2.4.1}
\]

(Here \( \Delta {R}_{jkla} \mathrel{\text{ := }} \left( {\Delta \mathrm{{Rm}}}\right) \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{j}},\frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{k}},\frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{l}},\frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{a}}}\right) \) .) Note that when considering expressions at the point \( p \) , where the vectors \( \left\{  \frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{i}}\right\} \) are orthonormal, we are able to use only lower indices, and the usual summation convention makes sense.

We focus on the second term of (2.4.1), since the third term differs only by a sign and a permutation of \( k \) and \( j \) . By the Ricci identity (2.1.2) we have

\[
{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}{R}_{kila} - {\nabla }_{j}{\nabla }_{i}{R}_{kila} =  - {R}_{jikc}{R}_{cila} - {R}_{jiic}{R}_{kcla} - {R}_{jilc}{R}_{kica} - {R}_{jiac}{R}_{kilc}.
\]

Now \( {R}_{jiic} =  - {R}_{jc} \) with our sign convention, and we have the first Bianchi identity \( {R}_{\text{ cila }} =  - {R}_{\text{ ilca }} - {R}_{\text{ lcia }} \) , and thus

\[
{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}{R}_{kila} - {\nabla }_{j}{\nabla }_{i}{R}_{kila} = {R}_{jikc}{R}_{ilca} + {R}_{jikc}{R}_{lcia} + {R}_{jc}{R}_{kcla}
\]

\[
- {R}_{jilc}{R}_{kica} - {R}_{jiac}{R}_{kilc}
\]

\[
= {R}_{jc}{R}_{kcla} + {B}_{jkla} - {B}_{jkal} + {B}_{jlka} - {B}_{jakl}.
\]

(2.4.2)

To handle the second term on the left-hand side of (2.4.2), we return to the second Bianchi identity, with permuted indices

\[
{\nabla }_{b}{R}_{laki} + {\nabla }_{l}{R}_{abki} + {\nabla }_{a}{R}_{blki} = 0,
\]

near \( p \) , and trace to give

\[
{g}^{bi}{\nabla }_{b}{R}_{kila} + {\nabla }_{l}{R}_{ak} - {\nabla }_{a}{R}_{lk} = 0.
\]

Applying \( {\nabla }_{j} \) and restricting our attention to \( p \) , we see that

\[
{\nabla }_{j}{\nabla }_{i}{R}_{kila} = {\nabla }_{j}{\nabla }_{a}{R}_{lk} - {\nabla }_{j}{\nabla }_{l}{R}_{ak},
\]

which may be plugged into (2.4.2) to give

\[
{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}{R}_{kila} = {\nabla }_{j}{\nabla }_{a}{R}_{lk} - {\nabla }_{j}{\nabla }_{l}{R}_{ak} + {R}_{jc}{R}_{kcla}
\]

\[
+ {B}_{jkla} - {B}_{jkal} + {B}_{jlka} - {B}_{jakl}.
\]

Finally, we apply this twice to (2.4.1) (once with \( k \) and \( j \) permuted) to conclude

\[
\Delta {R}_{jkla} =  - {\nabla }_{j}{\nabla }_{a}{R}_{lk} + {\nabla }_{j}{\nabla }_{l}{R}_{ak} + {\nabla }_{k}{\nabla }_{a}{R}_{lj} - {\nabla }_{k}{\nabla }_{l}{R}_{aj}
\]

\[
- {R}_{jc}{R}_{kcla} + {R}_{kc}{R}_{jcla} - 2\left( {{B}_{jkla} - {B}_{jkal} + {B}_{jlka} - {B}_{jakl}}\right) .
\]

Since, by definition,

\[
{M}_{ab} = \Delta {R}_{ab} - \frac{1}{2}{\nabla }_{a}{\nabla }_{b}R + 2{R}_{acdb}{R}_{cd} - {R}_{ac}{R}_{bc} + \frac{1}{2t}{R}_{ab}
\]

and we compute

\[
{\nabla }_{c}{P}_{cab} = {\nabla }_{c}\left( {{\nabla }_{c}{R}_{ab} - {\nabla }_{a}{R}_{cb}}\right)
\]

\[
= \Delta {R}_{ab} - {\nabla }_{c}{\nabla }_{a}{R}_{cb}
\]

\[
= \Delta {R}_{ab} - \frac{1}{2}{\nabla }_{a}{\nabla }_{b}R - {R}_{ad}{R}_{db} + {R}_{acdb}{R}_{cd},
\]

where we used the contracted second Bianchi identity, we may write \( {M}_{ab} \) in the form

(15.47)

\[
{M}_{ab} = {\nabla }_{c}{P}_{cab} + {R}_{acdb}{R}_{cd} + \frac{1}{2t}{R}_{ab}.
\]

This enables us to compute the evolution of \( {M}_{ab} \) using the evolution of \( {P}_{cab} \) previously derived. In particular, we may compute the evolution equation

of \( {\nabla }_{c}{P}_{cab} \) as follows. By formulas (15.35) and (15.45), we have

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {\nabla }_{c}{P}_{cab} = {\nabla }_{c}\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {P}_{cab} + 2{R}_{de}{\nabla }_{d}{P}_{eab}
\]

\[
+ 2{R}_{cdea}{\nabla }_{d}{P}_{ceb} + 2{R}_{cdeb}{\nabla }_{d}{P}_{cae}
\]

(15.48)

\[
= 2{\nabla }_{c}\left( {{R}_{cdea}{P}_{deb} + {R}_{cdeb}{P}_{dae} + {R}_{adeb}{P}_{cde} - {R}_{de}{\nabla }_{d}{R}_{caeb}}\right)
\]

\[
+ 2{R}_{de}{\nabla }_{d}{P}_{eab} + 2{R}_{cdea}{\nabla }_{d}{P}_{ceb} + 2{R}_{cdeb}{\nabla }_{d}{P}_{cae}
\]

(15.49)

\[
= 2{\nabla }_{c}{R}_{cdea}{P}_{deb} + 2{\nabla }_{c}{R}_{cdeb}{P}_{dae} + 2{R}_{cdea}{\nabla }_{c}{P}_{deb}
\]

\[
+ 2{R}_{cdeb}{\nabla }_{c}{P}_{dae} + 2{\nabla }_{c}{R}_{adeb}{P}_{cde} - 2{\nabla }_{c}{R}_{de}{\nabla }_{d}{R}_{caeb}
\]

\[
+ 2{R}_{adeb}{\nabla }_{c}{P}_{cde} - 2{R}_{de}{\nabla }_{c}{\nabla }_{d}{R}_{caeb} + 2{R}_{de}{\nabla }_{d}{P}_{eab}
\]

\[
+ 2{R}_{cdea}{\nabla }_{d}{P}_{ceb} + 2{R}_{cdeb}{\nabla }_{d}{P}_{cae}.
\]

To rewrite expression (15.49) in a better form, we apply a couple of formulas. First,

(15.50)

\[
{\nabla }_{c}{R}_{cdab} = {P}_{bad}
\]

by the second Bianchi identity. \( {}^{16} \) Second, ha regards to the term

\[
- 2{R}_{de}{\nabla }_{c}{\nabla }_{d}{R}_{\text{ caeb }}
\]

on the RHS of (15.49), we have

\[
{\nabla }_{c}{\nabla }_{d}{R}_{caeb} = {\nabla }_{d}{\nabla }_{c}{R}_{caeb} - {R}_{cdcf}{R}_{faeb} - {R}_{cdaf}{R}_{cfeb}
\]

\[
- {R}_{cdef}{R}_{cafb} - {R}_{cdbf}{R}_{caef}
\]

\[
= {\nabla }_{d}{P}_{bea} + {R}_{df}{R}_{faeb} - {R}_{dcaf}\left( {{R}_{cebf} + {R}_{cbfe}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {R}_{dcef}{R}_{acbf} - {R}_{dcbf}{R}_{acef}
\]

\[
= {\nabla }_{d}{P}_{bea} + {R}_{df}{R}_{faeb} - {B}_{daeb} + {B}_{dabe} - {B}_{deab} + {B}_{dbae},
\]

which follows from commuting \( {\nabla }_{c} \) and \( {\nabla }_{d} \) and then using equation (15.50) and the definition (15.38) of \( {B}_{abcd} \) . Applying these two identities to (15.48) and then grouping like terms, we have

(15.51)

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {\nabla }_{c}{P}_{cab} = 2{R}_{adeb}{\nabla }_{c}{P}_{cde} + 2{P}_{aed}{P}_{deb} + 2{P}_{bed}{P}_{dae}
\]

\[
+ 2{R}_{cdea}{\nabla }_{c}{P}_{deb} + 2{R}_{cdeb}{\nabla }_{c}{P}_{dae}
\]

\[
+ 2{R}_{cdea}{\nabla }_{d}{P}_{ceb} + 2{R}_{cdeb}{\nabla }_{d}{P}_{cae}
\]

\[
+ 2{\nabla }_{c}{R}_{adeb}{P}_{cde} - 2{\nabla }_{c}{R}_{de}{\nabla }_{d}{R}_{caeb}
\]

\[
- 2{R}_{de}\left( {-{B}_{daeb} + {B}_{dabe} - {B}_{deab} + {B}_{dbae}}\right)
\]

\[
- 2{R}_{de}{R}_{df}{R}_{faeb} + 2{R}_{de}\left( {{\nabla }_{d}{P}_{eab} - {\nabla }_{d}{P}_{bea}}\right) .
\]

Next,

\[
{R}_{cdea}\left( {{\nabla }_{c}{P}_{deb} + {\nabla }_{d}{P}_{ceb}}\right)  = \left( {{R}_{cdea} + {R}_{dcea}}\right) {\nabla }_{c}{P}_{deb} = 0,
\]

\[
{R}_{cdeb}\left( {{\nabla }_{c}{P}_{dae} + {\nabla }_{d}{P}_{cae}}\right)  = \left( {{R}_{cdeb} + {R}_{dceb}}\right) {\nabla }_{c}{P}_{dae} = 0,
\]

---

\( {}^{16} \) Indeed,

\[
{\nabla }_{c}{R}_{cdab} =  - {\nabla }_{a}{R}_{cdbc} - {\nabla }_{b}{R}_{cdca} =  - {\nabla }_{a}{R}_{db} + {\nabla }_{b}{R}_{da} = {P}_{bad}.
\]

---

which we obtained by relabeling \( c \) and \( d \) in the terms \( {R}_{cdea}{\nabla }_{d}{P}_{ceb} \) and \( {R}_{dceb}{\nabla }_{c}{P}_{dae} \) . This and

\[
{\nabla }_{c}{R}_{adeb}{P}_{cde} - {\nabla }_{c}{R}_{de}{\nabla }_{d}{R}_{caeb} = {\nabla }_{d}{R}_{aceb}\left( {{P}_{dce} + {\nabla }_{c}{R}_{de}}\right)
\]

\[
= {\nabla }_{d}{R}_{aceb}{\nabla }_{d}{R}_{ce}
\]

imply that we may rewrite (15.51) as

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {\nabla }_{c}{P}_{cab} = 2{R}_{adeb}{\nabla }_{c}{P}_{cde} + 2{R}_{de}\left( {{\nabla }_{d}{P}_{eab} + {\nabla }_{d}{P}_{eba}}\right)
\]

\[
+ 2{P}_{aed}{P}_{deb} + 2{P}_{bed}{P}_{dae} + 2{\nabla }_{d}{R}_{aceb}{\nabla }_{d}{R}_{ce}
\]

\[
- 2{R}_{de}\left( {-{B}_{daeb} + {B}_{dabe} - {B}_{deab} + {B}_{dbae}}\right)
\]

\[
+ 2{R}_{de}{R}_{df}{R}_{afeb}
\]

Using the Bianchi-type identity (15.6), we have

\[
2{P}_{aed}{P}_{deb} + 2{P}_{bed}{P}_{dae}
\]

\[
= \left( {{P}_{aed} + {P}_{dae}}\right) {P}_{deb} + 2{P}_{bed}{P}_{dae}
\]

\[
= {P}_{dea}{P}_{deb} - 2{P}_{bed}{P}_{ade}.
\]

This, relabeling indices, and the symmetry relations

(15.52)

\[
{B}_{abcd} = {B}_{cdab} = {B}_{badc} = {B}_{dcba}
\]

now imply that(15.53)

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {\nabla }_{c}{P}_{cab} = 2{R}_{acdb}{\nabla }_{e}{P}_{ecd} + 2{R}_{cd}\left( {{\nabla }_{c}{P}_{dab} + {\nabla }_{c}{P}_{dba}}\right)  + {P}_{cda}{P}_{cdb}
\]

\[
- 2{P}_{acd}{P}_{bdc} + 2{R}_{cd}{R}_{ce}{R}_{adeb} + 2{\nabla }_{e}{R}_{acdb}{\nabla }_{e}{R}_{cd}
\]

\[
+ 2{R}_{cd}\left( {{B}_{abcd} + {B}_{acbd} - {B}_{acdb} - {B}_{adcb}}\right) .
\]

The evolution equations of the other terms of \( {M}_{ab} \) are straightforward, namely

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) \left( {{R}_{acdb}{R}_{cd}}\right)  = \left( {\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {R}_{acdb}}\right) {R}_{cd} + {R}_{acdb}\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {R}_{cd}
\]

\[
- 2{\nabla }_{e}{R}_{acdb}{\nabla }_{e}{R}_{cd}
\]

(15.54)

\[
= 2{R}_{acdb}{R}_{cefd}{R}_{ef} - 2{\nabla }_{e}{R}_{acdb}{\nabla }_{e}{R}_{cd}
\]

\[
+ 2{R}_{cd}\left( {{B}_{acdb} - {B}_{acbd} + {B}_{adcb} - {B}_{abcd}}\right)
\]

and

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) \left( {\frac{1}{2t}{R}_{ab}}\right)  = 2{R}_{acdb}\left( {\frac{1}{2t}{R}_{cd}}\right)  - \frac{1}{2{t}^{2}}{R}_{ab}
\]

(15.55)

\[
= 2{R}_{acdb}\left( {{M}_{cd} - {\nabla }_{e}{P}_{ecd} + {R}_{cefd}{R}_{ef}}\right)  - \frac{1}{2{t}^{2}}{R}_{ab}.
\]

Thus, from (15.47) and the evolution equations (15.53), (15.54), and (15.55), we calculate

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {M}_{ab} = 2{R}_{acdb}{\nabla }_{e}{P}_{ecd} + 2{R}_{cd}\left( {{\nabla }_{c}{P}_{dab} + {\nabla }_{c}{P}_{dba}}\right)  + {P}_{cda}{P}_{cdb}
\]

\[
- 2{P}_{acd}{P}_{bdc} + 2{R}_{cd}{R}_{ce}{R}_{adeb} + 2{\nabla }_{e}{R}_{acdb}{\nabla }_{e}{R}_{cd}
\]

\[
+ 2{R}_{cd}\left( {{B}_{abcd} + {B}_{acbd} - {B}_{acdb} - {B}_{adcb}}\right)
\]

\[
+ 2{R}_{acdb}{R}_{cefd}{R}_{ef} - 2{\nabla }_{e}{R}_{acdb}{\nabla }_{e}{R}_{cd}
\]

\[
+ 2{R}_{cd}\left( {{B}_{acdb} - {B}_{acbd} + {B}_{adcb} - {B}_{abcd}}\right)
\]

\[
+ 2{R}_{acdb}\left( {{M}_{cd} - {\nabla }_{e}{P}_{ecd} - {R}_{cefd}{R}_{ef}}\right)  - \frac{1}{2{t}^{2}}{R}_{ab}
\]

\[
= 2{R}_{acdb}{M}_{cd} + 2{R}_{cd}\left( {{\nabla }_{c}{P}_{dab} + {\nabla }_{c}{P}_{dba}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {P}_{cda}{P}_{cdb} - 2{P}_{acd}{P}_{bdc} + 2{R}_{cd}{R}_{ce}{R}_{adeb} - \frac{1}{2{t}^{2}}{R}_{ab},
\]

where to obtain the last equality we canceled three pairs of terms.

Let \( X, Y, Z, W \) be arbitrary vector fields on \( M \) . Then

\[
\left( {{D}_{X, Z}^{2}\operatorname{Ric}}\right) \left( {Y, W}\right)  - \left( {{D}_{X, W}^{2}\operatorname{Ric}}\right) \left( {Y, Z}\right)
\]

\[
- \left( {{D}_{Y, Z}^{2}\operatorname{Ric}}\right) \left( {X, W}\right)  + \left( {{D}_{Y, W}^{2}\operatorname{Ric}}\right) \left( {X, Z}\right)
\]

\[
= \left( {\Delta R}\right) \left( {X, Y, Z, W}\right)  + Q\left( R\right) \left( {X, Y, Z, W}\right)
\]

\[
- \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k = 1}}^{n}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {X,{e}_{k}}\right) R\left( {{e}_{k}, Y, Z, W}\right)  - \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k = 1}}^{n}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Y,{e}_{k}}\right) R\left( {X,{e}_{k}, Z, W}\right) .
\]

Note that

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k = 1}}^{n}\left( {{D}_{X,{e}_{k}}^{2}R}\right) \left( {{e}_{k}, Y, Z, W}\right)  - \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k = 1}}^{n}\left( {{D}_{{e}_{k}, X}^{2}R}\right) \left( {{e}_{k}, Y, Z, W}\right)
\]

\[
= \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k, l = 1}}^{n}R\left( {X,{e}_{k},{e}_{k},{e}_{l}}\right) R\left( {{e}_{l}, Y, Z, W}\right)  + \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k, l = 1}}^{n}R\left( {X,{e}_{k}, Y,{e}_{l}}\right) R\left( {{e}_{k},{e}_{l}, Z, W}\right)
\]

\[
+ \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k, l = 1}}^{n}R\left( {X,{e}_{k}, Z,{e}_{l}}\right) R\left( {{e}_{k}, Y,{e}_{l}, W}\right)  + \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k, l = 1}}^{n}R\left( {X,{e}_{k}, W,{e}_{l}}\right) R\left( {{e}_{k}, Y, Z,{e}_{l}}\right) .
\]

Interchanging the roles of \( X \) and \( Y \) yields

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k = 1}}^{n}\left( {{D}_{Y,{e}_{k}}^{2}R}\right) \left( {{e}_{k}, X, Z, W}\right)  - \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k = 1}}^{n}\left( {{D}_{{e}_{k}, Y}^{2}R}\right) \left( {{e}_{k}, X, Z, W}\right)
\]

\[
= \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k, l = 1}}^{n}R\left( {Y,{e}_{k},{e}_{k},{e}_{l}}\right) R\left( {{e}_{l}, X, Z, W}\right)  + \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k, l = 1}}^{n}R\left( {Y,{e}_{k}, X,{e}_{l}}\right) R\left( {{e}_{k},{e}_{l}, Z, W}\right)
\]

\[
+ \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k, l = 1}}^{n}R\left( {Y,{e}_{k}, Z,{e}_{l}}\right) R\left( {{e}_{k}, X,{e}_{l}, W}\right)  + \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k, l = 1}}^{n}R\left( {Y,{e}_{k}, W,{e}_{l}}\right) R\left( {{e}_{k}, X, Z,{e}_{l}}\right) .
\]

We now subtract the second identity from the first. This implies

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k = 1}}^{n}\left( {{D}_{X,{e}_{k}}^{2}R}\right) \left( {{e}_{k}, Y, Z, W}\right)  - \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k = 1}}^{n}\left( {{D}_{Y,{e}_{k}}^{2}R}\right) \left( {{e}_{k}, X, Z, W}\right)
\]

\[
- \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k = 1}}^{n}\left( {{D}_{{e}_{k}, X}^{2}R}\right) \left( {{e}_{k}, Y, Z, W}\right)  + \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k = 1}}^{n}\left( {{D}_{{e}_{k}, Y}^{2}R}\right) \left( {{e}_{k}, X, Z, W}\right)
\]

\[
= \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k, l = 1}}^{n}\left\lbrack  {R\left( {X,{e}_{k}, Y,{e}_{l}}\right)  - R\left( {Y,{e}_{k}, X,{e}_{l}}\right) }\right\rbrack  R\left( {{e}_{k},{e}_{l}, Z, W}\right)
\]

\[
+ 2\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k, l = 1}}^{n}R\left( {X,{e}_{k}, Z,{e}_{l}}\right) R\left( {Y,{e}_{k}, W,{e}_{l}}\right)  - 2\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k, l = 1}}^{n}R\left( {X,{e}_{k}, W,{e}_{l}}\right) R\left( {Y,{e}_{k}, Z,{e}_{l}}\right)
\]

\[
- \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{l = 1}}^{n}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {X,{e}_{l}}\right) R\left( {{e}_{l}, Y, Z, W}\right)  + \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{l = 1}}^{n}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Y,{e}_{l}}\right) R\left( {{e}_{l}, X, Z, W}\right) .
\]

It follows from the first Bianchi identity that

\[
R\left( {X,{e}_{k}, Y,{e}_{l}}\right)  - R\left( {Y,{e}_{k}, X,{e}_{l}}\right)  = R\left( {X, Y,{e}_{k},{e}_{l}}\right) .
\]

Hence, we obtain

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k = 1}}^{n}\left( {{D}_{X,{e}_{k}}^{2}R}\right) \left( {{e}_{k}, Y, Z, W}\right)  - \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k = 1}}^{n}\left( {{D}_{Y,{e}_{k}}^{2}R}\right) \left( {{e}_{k}, X, Z, W}\right)
\]

\[
- \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k = 1}}^{n}\left( {{D}_{{e}_{k}, X}^{2}R}\right) \left( {{e}_{k}, Y, Z, W}\right)  + \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k = 1}}^{n}\left( {{D}_{{e}_{k}, Y}^{2}R}\right) \left( {{e}_{k}, X, Z, W}\right)
\]

\[
= Q\left( R\right) \left( {X, Y, Z, W}\right)
\]

\[
- \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{l = 1}}^{n}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {X,{e}_{l}}\right) R\left( {{e}_{l}, Y, Z, W}\right)  - \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{l = 1}}^{n}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Y,{e}_{l}}\right) R\left( {X,{e}_{l}, Z, W}\right) .
\]

Using the second Bianchi identity, we obtain

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k = 1}}^{n}\left( {{D}_{X,{e}_{k}}^{2}R}\right) \left( {{e}_{k}, Y, Z, W}\right)
\]

\[
= \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k = 1}}^{n}\left( {{D}_{X, Z}^{2}R}\right) \left( {{e}_{k}, Y,{e}_{k}, W}\right)  - \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k = 1}}^{n}\left( {{D}_{X, W}^{2}R}\right) \left( {{e}_{k}, Y,{e}_{k}, Z}\right)
\]

\[
= \left( {{D}_{X, Z}^{2}\mathrm{{Ric}}}\right) \left( {Y, W}\right)  - \left( {{D}_{X, W}^{2}\mathrm{{Ric}}}\right) \left( {Y, Z}\right) .
\]

Interchanging the roles of \( X \) and \( Y \) yields

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k = 1}}^{n}\left( {{D}_{Y,{e}_{k}}^{2}R}\right) \left( {{e}_{k}, X, Z, W}\right)
\]

\[
= \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k = 1}}^{n}\left( {{D}_{Y, Z}^{2}R}\right) \left( {{e}_{k}, X,{e}_{k}, W}\right)  - \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k = 1}}^{n}\left( {{D}_{Y, W}^{2}R}\right) \left( {{e}_{k}, X,{e}_{k}, Z}\right)
\]

\[
= \left( {{D}_{Y, Z}^{2}\operatorname{Ric}}\right) \left( {X, W}\right)  - \left( {{D}_{Y, W}^{2}\operatorname{Ric}}\right) \left( {X, Z}\right) .
\]

Moreover, the second Bianchi identity implies that

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k = 1}}^{n}\left( {{D}_{{e}_{k}, X}^{2}R}\right) \left( {{e}_{k}, Y, Z, W}\right)  - \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k = 1}}^{n}\left( {{D}_{{e}_{k}, Y}^{2}R}\right) \left( {{e}_{k}, X, Z, W}\right)
\]

\[
= \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k = 1}}^{n}\left( {{D}_{{e}_{k},{e}_{k}}^{2}R}\right) \left( {X, Y, Z, W}\right)  = \left( {\Delta R}\right) \left( {X, Y, Z, W}\right) .
\]

Putting these facts together, the assertion follows.

(Hamilton [65]). Let \( {g}_{ij}\left( t\right) ,0 \leq  t <  + \infty \) , be a noncollapsing nonsingular solution of the normalized Ricci flow on a compact three-manifold \( M \) . Then either

(i) there exist a sequence of times \( {t}_{k} \rightarrow   + \infty \) and a sequence of diffeomorphisms \( {\varphi }_{k} : M \rightarrow  M \) so that the pull-back of the metric \( {g}_{ij}\left( {t}_{k}\right) \) by \( {\varphi }_{k} \) converges in the \( {C}^{\infty } \) topology to a metric on \( M \) with constant sectional curvature; or

(ii) we can find a finite collection of complete noncompact hyperbolic three-manifolds \( {\mathcal{H}}_{1},\ldots ,{\mathcal{H}}_{m} \) with finite volume, and for all \( t \) beyond some time \( T <  + \infty \) we can find compact subsets \( {K}_{1},\ldots ,{K}_{m} \) of \( {\mathcal{H}}_{1},\ldots ,{\mathcal{H}}_{m} \) respectively obtained by truncating each cusp of the hyperbolic manifolds along constant mean curvature torus of small area, and diffeomorphisms \( {\varphi }_{l}\left( t\right) ,1 \leq  l \leq  m \) , of \( {K}_{l} \) into \( M \) so that as long as \( t \) sufficiently large, the pull-back of the solution metric \( {g}_{ij}\left( t\right) \) by \( {\varphi }_{l}\left( t\right) \) is as close as to the hyperbolic metric as we like on the compact sets \( {K}_{1},\ldots ,{K}_{m} \) ; and moreover if we call the exceptional part of \( M \) those points where they are not in the image of any \( {\varphi }_{l} \) , we can take the injectivity radii of the exceptional part at everywhere as small as we like and the boundary tori of each \( {K}_{l} \) are incompressible in the sense that each \( {\varphi }_{l} \) injects \( {\pi }_{1}\left( {\partial {K}_{l}}\right) \) into \( {\pi }_{1}\left( M\right) \) .
